There is some rust in the drivers side sill (see photograph) and there are a couple of minor dints - as might be expected of a car of this age. I has been repainted at some stage in it's life. description: Penned by Giorgetto Giugiaro at Bertone, the 105’s clean and distinctive design made it one of the most attractive small coupes of the 1960s and 70s and the earlier ‘Stepnose’ cars were the first of that body shape and seen as the most desirable.  As confirmed by Alfa Romeo our example is an RHD ‘Stepnose’ car delivered in 1969 to London, UK. It still wears it original delivery colour of AR209 ‘Musk’ green.  This car has had an engine change at some point to a later 1750 unit providing a useful increase in power and torque over the original. Not much is known about its earlier history, however we know it was in Australia from 1997 and with the 1750 motor in place, and we have a continuous history from that point. The car has always been local to Brisbane in QLD and has had 5 owners in that time. A decent folder of history and invoices accompanies the car with evidence of much expenditure over the last 25 years with little use during that time. The mileage in 2008 was 49,410, in 2012 it was 52,540 and it currently reads just 53,707.  Much of this work was focussed on improving performance and handling of the car and that certainly translates to a rewarding experience when driving it.  The current owner bought the car around 3 years ago and now needs to part with it due to a change in personal circumstances. During his ownership he has undertaken an extensive amount of work resulting in a car that is a blast to drive and looks the part too.   Recent work includes, new wiring loom, updated interior, new battery, reconditioned gearbox, rebuilt steering box, heavy duty Alfaholics sway bar, Aluminium radiator, new Alternator and oil cooler along with rebuilt Weber carbs. The engine benefits from a new crankshaft, bearings and general refresh.  To aid steering and handling the car has adjustable upper control arms, rose jointed drop links, lowered suspension with yellow Koni’s and ‘fast road’ springs. It is also fitted with a limited slip diff and in addition the rear upper spring mounts have been reinforced. The gearbox is excellent and a delight to use.  Turn the key and the engine fires up to a familiar Alfa growl. Out on the open road this car is just superb with the steering and braking being pin sharp. The induction noise from the race ‘trumpets’ is intoxicating and only adds to the on-road experience.  The paint although perfectly presentable from a distance, on close inspection shows areas of blistering due to moisture being in the primer when the topcoats were applied. Areas to the front and rear are fine and the roof too however patches of this blistering are present elsewhere. On the turret there are 2 small dents, however these might be able to be pulled out.  The GTA style wheels are from Campagnolo in Italy and are unmarked and like new. The tyres are just fitted and overall, they sit at the right height and look purposeful.   Once inside you are greeted by a new GTA style Hellebore steering wheel which looks superb. The dash has a new cover, and the classic gauges present very well. An interior from a later Series One 1750 GTV has been fitted to the car which includes the rare and desirable ‘flying buttress’ seats. They show no signs of rips or tears, and the tan colour works well with the ‘Musk’ green exterior.  Although the paint isn’t perfect, this is a sorted car and a driver’s delight which begs to be taken out in the hills for a good blast. The body is solid, and it looks wonderful on the GTA wheels and overall, there is a lot to like about this car.  All the stainless steel brightwork is in good order and the car is freshly serviced and ready for its new owner to enjoy.    .

description:
A very important Jaguar:

  • The 4th XK built – 660004
  • Perth delivered
  • Set WA speed record
  • First competition drive for an XK in the Southern Hemisphere
  • Star of Perth Motor Show
  • One owner since 1961
  • The most significant XK to come to the Australian market for years

The Jaguar XK series is renowned for bringing modernity to sports cars after World War 2. With a twin-cam 6-cylinder engine and sleek, stylish bodywork the XK120 broke new ground. The first 200 cars built were made with aluminium bodywork. These alloy cars are highly sought after today. Just 57 alloy body cars were built right hand drive.

This car was completed on 12 October 1949 and sold by M.S. Brooking, Perth.

Originally finished in a cream colour, shortly after taking delivery, the owner had the car repainted Luxor Blue, the corporate colour of the family business.

The XK120 competed at the Mundaring Hillclimb on 25 February 1950 – thus it became the first competition appearance of an XK in the Southern Hemisphere. In 1951 the Jaguar officially became the fastest car in WA, setting a new State record of 117.65 mph.

The car was shown at the Perth Motor Show in 1950 where unsurprisingly, it was the star attraction.

The Jaguar was bought by the present owner in February 1961. He was 21 years old at the time and has kept the car for the following 63 years.

Some changes have been made – motor (now a 4.2), gearbox, dashboard, windscreen, but all the original components have been kept.

The XK has appeared in newspaper and magazine features as well as books – and has been a popular exhibit at many events including the by-invitation Celebration of the Motorcar show.

Number stampings throughout the car prove its identity – chassis, engine, gearbox and body. Plus the car’s well-known and continuous provenance cannot be questioned. There is a great deal of historical documentation available for this car. Registered XKS 120P.

Opportunities to purchase such a historically significant car are few – don’t miss this opportunity.

description: The Jaguar S-type was launched in 1963 and was based on the styling of the Jaguar Mk2, which had been launched four years earlier.    At first glance there is little to tell the two apart, but an expert eye will be drawn to the extended rear bodywork, thinner chrome bumpers and larger indicators. Though a different model, the S-type was essentially an updated version of the Mk2 that featured numerous improvements first seen in the Jaguar MkX. The S-type would fill a niche for consumers who wanted all the technological improvements that came with the larger MkX, but in a smaller package similar to the Mk2.    Among the technological improvements on offer was the independent rear suspension system that was first seen on the MkX, which offered far superior road holding to the live rear axle system used in the Mk2. Though the suspension had changed, the engines stayed the same as in the Mk2 and XK models that came before.    The S-type was hailed as being a much more capable car, particularly in adverse weather conditions.In fact, the first and most significant wave of developments came only a year after the S-type entered production, in 1964.  In line with changing technology, the cross-ply tires were changed for radials, which gave the S-type even great road-holding, allowing spirited drivers to better exploit the advanced suspension setup. description: THE STORY  Making its debut at the 2005 Frankfurt Motor Show in Germany, the Jaguar XK X150 was the second and final generation of the Jaguar XK 2+2 grand tourer manufactured and marketed by British car manufacturer Jaguar Cars. It was notably designed by Jaguar’s chief designer Ian Callum, a prestigious car designer who has worked with Ford, TWR and Aston Martin.    The X150 features a bonded and riveted aluminium monocoque chassis with all-aluminium construction and bears a front grille styling reminiscent of the 1961 Jaguar E-Type sports car. It boasted a 32-valve 4.2L V8 engine mated to a 6-speed automatic transmission manufactured by ZF Friedrichshafen – the German technology company. Notably the interior featured steering-column mounted shift paddles.    Two body styles were available for the XK150 – a three-door fastback coupe and a two-door convertible.    THE CAR  Australian delivered by Barbagallo Jaguar in Perth WA on the 24th of January 2007, this example of a 2006 Jaguar XK X150 is finished in stunning Indigo Blue Pearl complimented by a Caramel leather interior.    There is a comprehensive service history for the vehicle including its time in WA and now in South Australian ownership, with the most recent service having been carried out by Classic and Sportscar Boutique of Norwood on the 20th of January 2024.    This XK X150 comes with a host of attractive features including ABS brakes, brake assist, front and rear parking sensors, 20” alloy wheels, cruise control, keyless start, rain-sensor wipers, a leather steering wheel and gear knob, central locking, power windows and 3-way memory power seats.    The 4.2L V8 engine is very strong – producing 219Kw of power and 411Nm of torque, and the 6-speed ZF automatic transmission boasts smooth gear changes. The exhaust note of this car is excellent.    This stylish Jaguar coupe is exceptionally fun to drive and shows only 90,020 kms on the clock – currently registered in SA.

description: Men of whatever age or means might do well to stay out of flirting range of this Mercedes 230SL. Lest they will become involved.    For this classy, sporty classic knows an uncanny lot about men and what it takes to make them fall in love with a fine motorcar.    And what a fine motorcar it is¦regard some of her charms that could very well turn the heads of the most respectable members of your community.    She was born and bred on the most wicked racecourses in the world and brought to sophisticated refinement on the speed limitless Autobahn and the boulevards of the worlds most renown capitals.    ABOUT THIS CAR        Introduced at the Geneva Salon in March 1963 as replacement for the 190SL, the 230SL abandoned its predecessor's four-cylinder engine in favour of a 2.3 liter fuel-injected six cylinder engine derived from that of the 220SE and producing 150bhp.      An instant classic, the body design was all-new while beneath the skin the running gear was conventional Mercedes-Benz, featuring all-round independent suspension (by swing axles at the rear), disc front/drum rear brakes.      Power steering.      This is an early model with the small sideway seat in the rear. This is known as the Kinder Seat, which was a factory option for these cars. It was coded as Option 565 on the data card.      Presented in a metallic red with black interior and a black soft top. Despite an expensive redesign with its Pininfarina styled roof, and refreshed cabin, some Big Cat enthusiasts felt that it was taking liberties with the classic looks of one of their favourites.    In fact, the Series III set out to rectify some of the deficiencies of the Series II, and was better equipped for everyday use, but you had to try one to find that out. In addition to new body panels, the new model had an increased amount of glass, and a much-needed additional 3 inch of headroom in the back - great if you're being chauffered!    External differences included flush door handles, vertical grille bars, revised 'Gothic' rear lamp clusters, and impact bumpers with decorative chrome along their top edges.    After early doubts were allayed, the Series III established itself as one of the best Jaguars of all time, with the injected 4.2-litre coming out as the pick of the crop. description:
The TD was the first post-war MG sports car which saw modernization of its pre-war design. As well as technical improvements, the TD boasted a more spacious cockpit than previous models.

With its overhead valve motor with twin carburettors, the MG TD 1250 was considered a spritely sports car in its day.

The earliest history of this car is not known, however the car had been with one Perth owner for more than 40 years – and the car was comprehensively restored not long before its long-term passed away. Following this, unfortunately, his wife threw away all the invoices of the restoration(!). But it is evident on inspection that every element of the car was restored, and to a high quality.

It spent the following decade in a collection, seldom being used and recently changed hands again.

It’s been through a comprehensive recommission by a Rolls-Royce-Bentley specialist company, with all necessary work done after its slumber. It has just passed a registration inspection, so a buyer can be confident it’s all good to go. It is presently on club license.

The pictures don’t show well enough how immaculate this car is throughout. The brightwork, trim, wet weather gear, internal and external hardware are all excellent and present impressively. It’s like a new car underneath.

description:
The Cabriolet version of Jaguar’s V12 grand tourer, this is the later model “HE” High Efficiency version of the XJS identifiable by its 5-spoke “Starfish” alloy wheels.

The XJ-SC has a ‘targa-type’ open roof, configurable in different ways. Only 3863 XJ-SCs were made with production ending in 1988. Most were produced for the US market with only a small proportion 950 right-hand drive – with just 191 coming to Australia.

This car was delivered new in Perth, to the daughter of WA tycoon Alan Bond in 1985. She took the car to New South Wales and later sold the car to a Sydney doctor. It then spent several years in Sydney, changing hands a couple more times.

The current Perth owner purchased the car in 2020 and had it returned to Perth. After arrival in Perth, major work was undertaken on the car. Some $14,000 was spent to ensure everything worked as it should. More work and servicing followed up most recently, in February 2025, the car had a minor service and oil change and fluids and safety check by a Jaguar specialist workshop.

This Jaguar drives well, with the engine pulling progressively and well with smooth gearchanges. Engine operating temperature and oil pressure are within specifications. The XJ-SC provides a smooth and relaxed drive – just as Jaguar intended.

The interior of the car presents well, with the burgundy leather upholstery and polished woodwork on the dash and doortrims.

Externally the car would benefit from some attention in small areas to return the car to a high standard.  Most of the paintwork presents well, so only localised repairs would be in order.

The air conditioning compressor and associated fittings have been removed. Some of the parts will be provided at sale. With the car is a set of correct boot lid (V-12 and XJ-SC) badges, original toolkit and two workshop manuals.

This car has seen minimal use over the past five years. It shares a garage with another Jaguar. The odometer shows 176,000km. This lack of use has precipitated the car’s sale. This is not a show car and has been priced accordingly. The cosmetic items needed could be done over time, or at home by an enthusiast.

It’s the owner’s intention to retain the number plates GR 003.

The XJ-SC should provide a new owner many years of motoring pleasure. A usable everyday classic, with all the luxury and performance which the model stood out with back when it was new. There is excellent service and parts support for the model and an active Jaguar Car Club to help you maximise your enjoyment.

description: THE STORY  The Mercedes-Benz 300SEL started its life as a private venture in 1966 by company engineer Erich Waxenberger. His goal was to take the powerful 6.3L M100 V8 engine from the massive Mercedes-Benz 600 saloon and limousine and fit it into the engine bay of the top-end 6-cylinder 300SEL W109 model. This resulted in a prototype boasting an impressive level of performance for the time, a nearly two-ton luxury sports sedan with muscle car power - the fastest sedan in the world for several years.    Following on from the strong reception of the limited production 300SEL 6.3, Mercedes-Benz offered an all-new 3.5L M116 V8 engine with new Bosch D-Jetronic electronic fuel injection in 1969. The car was offered with a 4-speed automatic transmission with fluid coupling.     In addition to its excellent performance, the 300SEL was incredibly luxurious for the time, equipped with features including air-suspension, ventilated 4-wheel power disc brakes, power windows, central locking and power steering. Optional features included air conditioning, a power sunroof, an audio tape deck, rear window curtains and writing tables and reading lamps.    AMG today is the high-performance division of Mercedes-Benz, but back then was a small local tuning workshop founded by two former Mercedes engineers. They modified a makeshift variant of the 300SEL to compete in racing events. The vehicle was nicknamed “Red Sow” and finished second in the ’24 Hours of Spa’ endurance racing event in 1971. At the end of its racing career, the car was sold to the French company ‘Matra’, which used the vehicle for tests of jet-fighter landing gear.     THE CAR  Delivered to Australia in Sydney on the 22nd of October in 1970, this 1970 Mercedes-Benz 300SEL 3.5 is in fantastic condition with only 66,082 kms on the clock.    She is finished in stunning White (paint code 050) which stands out beautifully against the gleaming chrome trim, badging and front grille.     The interior of this car is immaculate - featuring brand new mint condition leather seats, tasteful olive carpeting throughout and a burled walnut dash, along with wood-grain trim along the door cards.   Built as a luxury vehicle for 1970, the car is equipped with power steering, power windows, central locking and factory air-conditioning. An aftermarket Alpine head unit has been installed with Bluetooth functionality.    Mechanically, the Bosch D-Jetronic fuel-injected 3.5L V8 engine is strong and puts power to the road via a four-speed automatic transmission with fluid coupling. She boasts a smooth ride thanks to self-levelling air suspension and 4-wheel power-assisted disc brakes for stopping power.    This car has been registered in NSW, VIC and is currently on historic registration in SA. The original owner’s manual and documentation are supplied with purchase.

description: 1988 Porsche 930 Turbo ** SLANT NOSE ** Cabriolet, original matching Numbers, factory certified by factory Porsche Vin decoder option list, the authentic real thing, this is rarest Porsche 911 and a piece of Porsche design history, opportunely to add to your Porsche collection with massive investment potential, exceptionally rare and highly coveted, This exemplifies the quintessential classic 1980s exotic style poster car.    The Porsche 930 Turbo Slant Nose came with the M505 option code and is as among the rarest 911 models, revered by motorsport enthusiasts as one of the most desirable variant of the 911 lineup. With only 948 units ever produced, the Porsche 930 Turbo Flachbau ( SLANT NOSE ) emerges as one of the scarcest 911 models. Paired with exclusive individual colors and interiors, these vehicles have captivated collectors' attention.    In the final generation of the Porsche 930 Turbo, notable changes included a shift in option code designations. For the US market, M505 denoted the Porsche 930 Slantnose, leading to the adoption of the standard 930 Turbo front apron in the M505 Porsche 911 Slantnose, with an additional oil cooler placed in the rear right fender. description: A Timeless Classic Experience the elegance and performance of this 1971 Mercedes Benz 280S, W108. This stunning 280S is finished in its original and highly desirable hue of Blue (code 903H) over a cream ‘MB-Tex’ leatherette trim, complemented by its original dark blue carpets and handsome wood veneer inlays on the dashboard and windows. Key Features: Exceptional Presentation: This Mercedes-Benz 280 S is a beautifully presented example of the marque’s classic saloon. The previous owner meticulously repainted it in its original colour, drawing constant admiration for its amazing bodywork and gleaming finish. Historic Significance: Introduced at the Frankfurt Motor Show in 1965, the W108 series set a new standard for mass-produced luxury saloons. Designed by the renowned Paul Bracq, also known for the iconic Mercedes Benz W113 Pagoda, the W108 series embodies luxury and timeless design. Engine and Performance: From 1967 to 1972, the second series of Mercedes Benz W108’s featured the upgraded 2.8-litre (M130 engine series) inline 6-cylinder overhead cam engines. The 280S boasts two twin-barrel downdraft Zenith carburettors, while the 280S is equipped with mechanical Bosch injection. Known for its reliability and durability, this model is a sought-after collector's car today. Condition: Interior and Exterior: While the car is generally in excellent condition, there are a few points to note. There is a small tear on the driver’s seat and some patina on the chrome exterior finishes. The power steering has a leak (red fluid), which I believe needs attention. The original vacuum central locking still works but loses pressure, so manual unlocking of the passenger doors is required upon returning to the vehicle. Driving Experience: Beyond these minor issues, the car presents and drives beautifully. It retains the simplicity of steel coil springs and oil-filled shock absorbers, as opposed to the more complex self-levelling air suspension. Historical Production: The W108.016 was produced between November 1967 and September 1972, with a total of 93,666 examples made. This particular model features a smooth inline 2.8 L 6-cylinder engine, offering a timeless driving experience. The vehicle is currently in storage, and I will post some better photos soon. This is a rare opportunity to own a piece of automotive history that combines classic style with legendary performance. Inspections welcomed, first to see will buy! Don’t miss your chance to own this exceptional classic Mercedes Benz!

description: Penned by Giorgetto Giugiaro at Bertone, the 105’s clean and distinctive design is one of the most attractive small coupes of the 1960s and 70s. The 1750 GTV was the first evolution of the original design and benefited from Alfa Romeo’s larger 1779cc engine in addition to many other updates and modifications including to the chassis, suspension and brakes. It made for a much better driving car particularly at higher touring speeds and ensured the cars performance was better than many sports cars of the era. Arguably the ‘1750’ motor is regarded by enthusiasts as the one to have given its combination of power, torque and free revving nature.  Externally the 1750 GTV also departed from the earlier cars with a new nose styling incorporating a revised grill with four headlamps.  Our example is an early Series 1 model delivered in April 1968 to Pymble NSW, as confirmed by the Certificate of Origin which accompanies the car. According to the ‘FUSI’ records its chassis number of 1450004 suggests it’s the 4th one produced underlining how early it is.  It has been in the ownership of known ‘Alfisti’ who have kept it in wonderful order. The current owner acquired the car in 2006 and commenced a restoration in 2009. The car was then completed and registered in 2018 and has covered under 2,000 miles since that time.  During the restoration the car underwent a back to metal repaint, extensive mechanical and electrical work. It still presents extremely well to this day. The body is in very good all-round condition with minimal panel work being required once the paint was removed. There are some stone chips and marks on the body due to age, but none are significant. The car had a colour change by its previous owner to red from its original Biancospino but it suits the car well. The interior is in the original Nero.   All the stainless steel brightwork is in wonderful order and sets the car off beautifully. The wheels although from a later model 2000 GTV are refurbished and are in perfect condition.  The interior is just lovely with everything as it should be. An unmarked steering wheel greets you and the dash and dials are something that just looks perfect to the eye. The dash has been restored at some point and the current dash pad is well made and is a practical addition. The desirable ‘flying buttress’ seats have been reupholstered and are just a lovely feature.  The instrument binnacle looks spot on with only a little frosting to the rev counter cover, but this is being picky. The headlining is fresh and perfect to the eye. The timber veneer to the centre console is not original but a good match and is well fitted. The carpets are new and unmarked.  Turn the key and the engine fires up to a familiar Alfa growl. Out on the open road this car is just superb. The gearbox is excellent with no issues with the synchro’s. It is accurate, smooth, and quick to work through the gears and using it is quite addictive. The engine is responsive and pulls extremely well benefiting from the carbs being rebuilt and tuned.  The engine bay is clean and largely original. The boot is excellent and lined with carpet.  These 105’s are great driver’s cars, and we can see why they are so sought after. Freshly restored cars are still fetching well north of $100,000 and this car represents good buying. The car will be serviced and ready to be enjoyed by its new owner.

description: THE STORY  Unveiled at the Geneva Motor Show in 2007, the first generation of the Maserati GranTurismo set a record for the most quickly developed car in the auto industry – going from design to production in just nine months.    The architecture of the GranTurismo was a derivative of Maserati’s M139 platform from their fifth generation Quattriporte, with a shortened wheelbase and rear overhang. The engine was pushed back beyond the front wheels centerline and the chassis was constructed of stamped and boxed steel sections complimented by two aluminium subframes – one at the front supporting the engine and a tubular one at the rear supporting suspension and the differential.    The first generation GranTurismo came equipped with a 4.2L (256ci) V8 Ferrari-sourced engine and two transmission options – a conventional torque converter 6-speed automatic or a 6-speed automated manual gearbox.    THE CAR  Australian delivered to Frewville SA on the 14th of March in 2008, this example of a 2008 Maserati GranTurismo is in outstanding condition with only 51,875 kms on the clock.    The car is finished in classic ‘Grigio Touring’ Silver with a striking ‘Rosso Corallo’ red leather interior.    Equipped with a 4.2L (256ci) V8 Ferrari-Maserati F136 U naturally aspirated engine, she boasts outstanding power and a wonderful exhaust note. The 6-speed ZF 6HP 26 automatic transmission features an Auto Sports Mode function and an ICE mode function for low-grip road conditions.    The car is also equipped with Maserati’s ‘Skyhook’ suspension system – an electronic suspension system that uses sensors to monitor the road conditions and vehicle movements in order to adjust the damping of each shock absorber in real time to provide a smooth and comfortable ride.    Other features of this vehicle include cruise control, rain-sensing wipers, heated power front seats, heated mirrors, remote keyless entry, dual-zone climate control, power windows, power steering, rear parking sensors, a full colour display multimedia head unit with in-built navigation and a premium BOSE sound system.    This car has been lovingly looked after in SA since its delivery, and a full service history is included alongside the original owner’s manuals and documentation.    Immaculate inside and out, this Maserati GranTurismo is exceptionally stylish and incredibly fun to drive.

description: *** We are open for business by appointment***  *** Please phone first to make sure someone is here to help you with your enquiry***  One of very few Jaguar XJ13 Replicas in the world, (5 speed manual) of the ``One and Only``, which resides in a Museum in the UK.  Built using Jaguar's original plans (supplied by Jaguar) by John Wilson (Vehicle Engineer in the Canberra/Sydney region) and first road registered in the ACT in 1986.  Not so much a replication but a re-creation of the original, even down to the identical wheels (the only set surviving from the original casting).   The body panels use the identical grade of alloy rivets used in the building of the Concorde (which were also used in the original XJ13)   It also uses the identical glass for the screens, plexiglas side and rear, and the V12 engine features four camshafts, as in the original, plus the ZF Transaxle gearbox is mounted upside down (as was the original).  Brakes and suspension are also Jaguar.  Has been Dyno Tuned and measured at 700HP at the flywheel!!  Recently track tested at the Tailem Bend SA race track and surpassed all expectations.  Recently won Best Vehicle out of 900 at the All British Day in Adelaide ( Feb 2018), and was voted Joint Winner of the recent National Jaguar Rally at Birdwood National Motor Museum, SA, April 2018.  Norman Dewis drove this car in July 2004 and commented on how close it drove to the original.  ( Photos of him in and with the car included).  It has been involved in many events including Targa Tasmania, The Dutton Rally, Geelong to Adelaide Rally, 1990 Aust F1 Grand Prix, 2012 Melbourne F1 Grand prix, Classic Adelaide Rally (twice), the Shannons Classic Car Demonstration, The Pebble Beach rally and numerous North American Jaguar meets.  This Re-creation in our opinion, totally eclipses all previous XJ13 replicas offered for sale, and given that it was 15 years in the making, with around $200k U.S. reportedly spent on the engine alone - and can be road registered - make this car another ``One and Only``!

description: Just arrived - this 1967 Lancia Fulvia has been upgraded to a Rallye 1.3 HF Tribute. The Fulvia, replacement to the Appia, had success in the racing industry, with Fulvias winning the Italian Rally Championships each year from 1965 to 1973 and the International Rally Championship in 1972. Switching to front wheel drive, the Fulvias ran independent suspension in the front using wishbones and a single leaf spring, while a beam axle with a Panhard rod and leaf springs sat in the rear. The Fulvia also received Dunlop disc brakes and the V4 motors were bored out to reach 1,298cc and paired with a 4 speed manual transmission. This car is Australian delivered and, in the 1990's was built in tribute to those Championship winning cars. The restoration saw the Lancia receiving the correct HF paint scheme with Turin stripe, decals and badges. Additionally fitted are Lancia alloy HF Cromodora rims, correct HF wheel arches, a quick-fill fuel cap, and a black lightweight interior. The standard 1.3 Fulvia engine has received some rare 1.3HF parts in its restoration, and all servicing and mechanical work since has been performed by Eurosport in Kent town. The car remains neat and tidy but still an older restoration, ready to drive and have fun on the windy hills roads that it was built for. Interior photos to come. description: Penned by Giorgetto Giugiaro at Bertone, the 105’s clean and distinctive design made it one of the most attractive small coupes of the 1960s and 70s and the earlier ‘Stepnose’ cars were the first of that body shape and seen as the most desirable.    As confirmed by Alfa Romeo our example is an RHD Australian ‘Stepnose’ car delivered in 1967 to Alec Mildren Pymble, NSW.    This car has had an engine change at some point to a later 1750 unit providing a useful increase in power and torque over the original. Its also had modifications to reflect a GTA look including the signature wheels, removal of bumpers and a GTA front end grill.    The current owner bought the car from us around a year ago and now needs to part with it due to a change in personal circumstances. During his ownership he has undertaken some mechanical work such as carb tuning, new water pump, hoses and belts.    The previous is well know to us and owned the car for 7 years and at that point had the car recommissioned with work to the brakes, suspension, carbs and a number of other items throughout the car including the fitment of an Alfaholics dual circuit braking system with rebuilt large ATE front callipers. This work was completed by a know expert with Alfa Romeo 105’s.    Turn the key and the engine fires up to a familiar Alfa growl. Out on the open road this car is just superb. We have been informed that when the engine was rebuilt  and Autodelta racing cams were fitted although there is no proof of this. However, the engine really comes alive after 2000 rpm and certainly invites some spirited driving and is a blast to drive. The gearbox is good with only a small issue on second gear, but this is not significant it can easily be driven without any crunch occurring. It does however jump out of reverse gear and the gear lever needs holding however is perfectly drivable as is and has been this way since the current owner bought the car. A compression test shows excellent results on all cylinders.    The car has been resprayed in an attractive shade of dark red, however it is not the correct Alfa Romeo red as originally delivered. The paint although perfectly presentable from a distance on close inspection it shows areas of blistering due to moisture being in the primer when the topcoats were applied. The front of the car is fine and the roof too however patches of this blistering are present elsewhere.    The GTA replica wheels are from Classic Alfa in the UK and are unmarked and like new. The tyres are fresh and overall, they sit at the right height and look the part. The handling of the car is excellent in part due to the work done to the suspension and brakes.    Inside a fresh carpet set has been fitted which is lovely along with a new Momo California steering wheel. The dash shows the usual cracking but is original. All the seats are very good and show no signs of rips or tears.    This is no show queen and could benefit from some tidy-ups in a few areas, however this is a sorted car and a driver’s delight which begs to be taken out in the hills for a good blast. The body is solid, and it looks wonderful on the GTA wheels and overall, there is a lot to like about this car, particularly given the asking price.    All the stainless steel brightwork is available and comes with the car along with invoices for recent work done by the current owner.    These 105’s are great driver’s cars, and we can see why they are so sought after. Freshly restored cars are still fetching well north of $100,000 and this car represents good buying and to enjoy as is. The car is serviced, on the button and ready to go.

description:
The all-new C215 hardtop coupé range was launched in February 2000, alongside its sedan sibling in W/V220-series S-Class form. Designed by Australian Peter Arcadipane in collaboration with Daimler-Benz design legend Bruno Sacco, the C215 is widely regarded as one of the most beautiful coupés ever produced by the Stuttgart marque. Its flowing, elegant lines and distinctive proportions paid homage to past classics like the W111 coupé, while presenting a thoroughly modern and unique presence on the road at the turn of the century.

This stunning April 2002-complied CL500 is finished in Zircon Silver (code 744) with a charcoal perforated leather interior, complemented by rich burr walnut timber trim throughout the cabin. It has travelled just 141,535km and was delivered new by Mercedes-Benz McIntosh of Mosman. It comes complete with its original factory literature, spare remote key, owner's wallet and service log book. The log book reflects a fastidious service history, with maintenance carried out exclusively by the selling dealer through to 2022, and subsequently by respected independent specialists.

This CL500 was retained by its original owner until late 2024, having relocated to Queensland in 2021, where it received two additional services before being acquired by a Mercedes-Benz enthusiast in Sydney. We have now acquired the vehicle from this collector, and it is currently registered in NSW until January 2026.

This is one of the finest examples of the C215 series we have encountered in recent years, and we are confident that its condition – inside and out – will satisfy even the most discerning buyer. The Zircon Silver paintwork retains a deep, consistent lustre, and the leather interior remains soft, supple, and free from excessive wear – clear indicators of careful ownership and garage storage throughout its life.

As expected of a Mercedes-Benz of this calibre – with a new-car driveaway price approaching $300,000 in 2002 – this CL500 is generously equipped even by today’s standards. Highlights include electrically-adjustable front seats with memory, heating and ventilation, dual-zone climate control, electric sunroof, keyless entry, electric steering column adjustment, a concert-quality 11-speaker sound system, soft-close doors, COMAND with satellite navigation, rain-sensing wipers, walnut and leather steering wheel, Xenon headlights, front and rear parking sensors, electric rear blind, and the sophisticated ABC (Active Body Control) hydraulic active suspension system.

Power comes from the naturally-aspirated 5.0L V8 engine, developing 225kW and 470Nm of torque. Mated to a 5-speed automatic transmission and driving the rear wheels via ASR and Electronic Stability Program, the CL500 delivers seamless performance with minimal fuss. It can sprint from 0 to 100km/h in just 6.5 seconds – impressive for a grand tourer of this size and refinement.

The car has a commanding presence on the road, further enhanced by its factory 17-inch 5-spoke alloy wheels shod in premium Pirelli tyres.

We unreservedly recommend this exceptional C215-series CL500 to the Mercedes-Benz enthusiast or the discerning buyer seeking an exclusive, elegant and increasingly collectible four-seat GT coupé. Its originality, low mileage and exemplary condition will not disappoint, and the documented service history is a testament to its meticulous upkeep over the past two decades.

description: THE STORY  Produced between 2004 and 2011, the Ferrari 612 Scaglietti was an executive 2+2 coupe grand tourer designed to replace the smaller Ferrari 456.    The design of the large side scallops and the headlights pay homage to the Ferrari 375 MM built in 1954 – a car commissioned by director Roberto Rossellini for his wife, Ingrid Bergman.    The chassis of the 612 is made entirely from aluminium, consisting of a space frame with an aluminium body welded on.    Two choices of transmission were available for the 612, a 6-speed manual or a 6-speed automated manual paddle shift. In 2007 Ferrari announced new features for the 612 - the ‘SuperFast’ robotic (F1) gearbox and a new electro-chromatic glass roof that could tint and lighten at the push of a button.    In 2008 Ferrari unveiled the One-to-One (OTO) personalization program and from then, the Ferrari 612 was only available through this special-order process. The OTO program allowed clients to hand-pick a wide variety of options for their vehicle, from leather swatches to brake calipers, and everything in between.    THE CAR  Australian delivered, this 2008 Ferrari 612 Scaglietti is in immaculate condition and has an extremely low 16,550 kilometers on the clock. Finished in gorgeous Nero Daytona, she has a full black leather interior complimented by distinctive yellow double-stitching throughout.    From the outside this car looks incredibly sleek – the metallic black paintwork is contrasted wonderfully with the yellow Ferrari badging and the bright yellow brake calipers attached to the 20” polished chrome ‘Challenge’ alloy wheels.    The interior is exceptionally clean and well-kept, and is equipped with a lot of features from the Ferrari OTO personalization program – a panoramic electro-chromatic glass roof with an electronic tinting function, a reverse camera with widescreen view, reverse parking guidance, front and rear parking sensors, multi-adjustable comfort ‘Daytona’ sports seats, a BOSE multimedia interface connected to premium BOSE HIFI sound, iPod connectivity, a TV tuner, a navigation system and a factory upgraded window tint package.    Mechanically this Ferrari boasts a 5.7L (357ci) V12 engine with a compression ratio of 11:1  - this car can accelerate from 0-100km/h in just four seconds, as well as attain a top speed of 320km/h. She also comes equipped with the Ferrari ‘SuperFast’ robotic (F1) gearbox, GTS suspension, a sport exhaust and carbon ceramic brakes. Handling is a dream and there’s nothing like the famed roar of a Ferrari exhaust note.    With only 3,025 built world-wide, and one of only a handful delivered to Australia – Ferrari’s sporting V12 engines are becoming increasingly sought after by collectors. This is a perfect example of ‘Drive your Dream’.

One of the most spectacular, exciting classic and exotic supercars we have ever had the privilege of offering for sale; the most iconic Lamborghini automobile ( A must have in any collection ).    This 1981 Lamborghini Countach LP400 S left the Lamborghini Santa Agata factory on November 5th 1980 and arrived in Melbourne in the original colour of Rame Colorado and Senape tan colour interior, the car was ordered in February 1979 with the following options, lowered seats for both driver and passenger, forward pedals, fitted with a rear spoiler and specially ordered with factory gold badges.  At some time between 1985 and 1993 the colour of the Countach changed to a stunning White pearlescent and retained the pristine perfect Original Senape Tan leather interior. This Countach is a truly collectable supercar and the most recognised 80s poster car, idolised by everybody and now enjoys a new generation of automotive art appreciation.    The Lamborghini Countach LP400 S, particularly the 1981 model, is an iconic representation of automotive engineering and design from the 1980s. Introduced in the early 1970s, the Countach set new standards for supercars with its radical styling and advanced engineering. The 1981 LP400 S model is especially notable for its striking angular design, characterized by sharp lines and a wedge-shaped body, which became a hallmark of Lamborghini's design language Designo Bertone.    Under the hood, the Countach LP400 S boasts a 4.0-liter V12 engine, delivering around 355 horsepower. This powerful engine, paired with a five-speed manual transmission, enables the car to reach top speeds of over 180 mph, making it one of the fastest cars of its era. The performance of the LP400 S is complemented by its lightweight tubular space frame and aluminum body panels, which contribute to its impressive speed and agility.    Inside, the Countach LP400 S offers a driver-focused cockpit with minimalistic yet luxurious features. The seating position is low, enhancing the driving experience and providing a sense of connection with the road. Despite its raw power and aggressive design, the Countach is also renowned for its precision handling and responsive steering.    Overall, the 1981 Lamborghini Countach LP400 S remains a celebrated and highly sought-after classic, embodying the spirit of innovation and performance that defines the Lamborghini brand. description: THE STORY Manufactured in 1971, the Volkswagen Type 2 ``Microbus`` Samba was the top-tier version of VW’s second-generation Transporter lineup - often referred to as the ``T2a`` or ``Early Bay”. With its iconic panoramic windows, distinctive two-tone paintwork, and roof-mounted sunroof panels, the Samba model became an enduring symbol of freedom and exploration during the 1960s and early 1970s. The Samba’s most distinguishing features were its 21 or 23 windows (depending on configuration), which included eight skylight windows integrated into the roof and stylish “jail bar” trim in the rear. A large canvas sunroof was standard on most models, designed to open the cabin to the sky—perfect for scenic drives along the coast or cross-country road trips. The 1971 model year marked the end of the simpler “Early Bay” era, before the 1972 introduction of more heavily regulated bumper designs and other structural changes. Today, well-preserved examples of the ’71 Microbus Samba are considered among the most collectible of Volkswagen’s classic vans, prized for their purity of design, cultural significance and timeless charm. THE CAR Imported into Queensland in 2021, this fantastic left-hand drive 1971 Volkswagen Microbus Samba was immediately purchased by the current South Australian owner. This Microbus is stunning and is presented in its original paint colour of Orange Red and Chocolate Brown with a beige interior trim. Both the paint the interior are in outstanding, restored condition. A true example of a lovingly restored classic, this car has been treated to a suite of upgrades. The original 1.5 litre engine has been replaced with a brand new S41 1.835 litre (109ci) VW engine which has travelled just over 2,000kms since replacement. The 4-speed manual gearbox has been fully rebuilt, and the front wheels have been upgraded with disc brakes for enhanced braking performance. The inside of this Microbus is a striking blend of vintage style and modern comfort with the inclusion of new curtains, a custom sound system with radio and the subwoofers and amplifier hidden under the seats. A fantastic wooden steering wheel has been added as have custom cup holders, USB ports, a refrigerator and a built-in wooden shelf with LED lighting where miniature Kombi Van models are currently displayed (included with purchase). There is also a dual-battery setup to accommodate the additional power required for all the accessories. The roof of the vehicle features a Webasto-style folding sunroof that spans most of the length of the vehicle. There are two aluminium roof-racks that currently house a vintage-styled surfboard which is included with the sale. Also included is a wonderful 1950’s aluminium suitcase. A head-turner wherever she goes, this custom VW Microbus Samba is a true collector’s dream. Currently on historic registration in SA.

description: The W108/109 S-Class saloon was the pinnacle of luxury car design from the time of its introduction in 1965, featuring stylish, classical lines by Paul Bracq, a roomy and beautifully appointed interior and was powered by a range of six-cylinder engines. Demand from the American market for more power saw the introduction in 1970 of a V8 model with the new M116 3.5-litre engine featuring a single-overhead camshaft per bank, Bosch fuel injection and a healthy 200bhp on tap. In the best tradition of Stuttgart's finest, the S-Class boasted state of the art safety equipment, roadholding and luxury features and was built to the highest standards. Offering effortless performance, the 280 SE 3.5 was usually equipped with a four-speed automatic transmission using a fluid flywheel but a small number were sold with the four-speed manual. In production for just two full years, the 280 SE 3.5 was built in limited numbers and just 11,309 were built in total - the vast majority of these going to North America and surviving examples are few and far between in Australia. This 1970 Mercedes-Benz 280SEL 3.5 is finished in silver over a red interior and is powered by a 3.5-litre V8 paired with a floor shift automatic transmission. Features include 14″ steel wheels, air conditioning and a Becker radio. The car reportedly spent much of its life in Victoria and was subsequently relocated to South Australia. Recent work has since included servicing the rear brakes along with an oil change and a replacement thermostat and valve cover gaskets. The seats and door panels are trimmed in re MB-Tex, and the interior features a contrasting black dash with immaculate woodgrain inserts as well as darker red carpeting. Amenities include air conditioning, a rear window defroster, a clock, and floor mats. The dash and associated woodwork is in excellent condition with no fading and minimal wear is evident on the headliner, upholstery, and interior brightwork as shown in the gallery. The Becker radio is fully functional, however the air conditioning will need a re-gas. Mechanically this car is in superb condition and has benefitted from a recent major service. The fuel injection system works perfectly with the car starting well and running very smoothly even from cold. With all major wear items such as brakes, cooling hoses, shocks and tyres replaced in recent years, this is a car with very little to spend. Paint and body work is as good as you will find on a car of this age, with zero rust and only small paint imperfections. Chromework is stunning and this presentation coupled to such a beautiful interior means this is a very rare find.

description: DON’T BUY THIS CAR! * If you are a hoon. * If you are a collector who hides your gems in your garage. The SLK-55 is a DRIVABLE COLLECTIBLE SPORTS CAR! * If you are an introvert who doesn't want to be approached by people all the time to talk about your car. * If you are NOT an investor. This up-and-coming collectible will likely join the ranks of the 1955 300SL and the 1970 280SL Pagoda Roadster. On the rare occasions when one comes on the market the price it’s always more expensive than the last. * If feeling like a race car driver is not your thing. * If you don’t enjoy the roar of a naturally aspirated 5.5 l V 8 hand-built “and signed” engine cold start in the morning. * If you are NOT extremely picky. THIS SLK-55 IS ONE OF ONLY TWO FOR SALE IN THE COUNTRY! WHY DID I BUY THIS CAR? I once had a LJ GTR Torona, which gave me the same sensation as the SLK-55. Except that it was actively trying to kill me. In comparison, the SLK 55 stops when you want to stop, corners when you want to corner and... F*CKING FLIES. It’s sheer motoring joy. *_* It’s got all the things that the Torona didn’t: - Active traction control. - Airbags. - Vented disc brakes. - Reliability. And then the price! Put in this way: Torana will give you: * The thrills. * The collectability. For $100k +. Mercedes will give you: * The thrills. * The collectability. * THE DRIVABILITY. * THE SAFETY. For $95k. REVIEWED BY JEREMY CLARKSON ON TOP GEAR. After this review, he went out and bought one! “If you squint a bit, the SLK looks like the giant-killing McLaren Mercedes SLR. And if you go for the 55 AMG, it goes like the SLR too. Sort of. Its 5.5 liter engine might lack the supercharger that makes other AMG-tuned cars shred tarmac, but the SLK 55 is light so it doesn’t need the boost. It sounds like an American muscle car, goes like a rocket and handles well in a brutish way. It also comes with a retractable hard top, making it probably the most complete sports car available. Which is why I bought one.” SPECS The SLK 55 (R171) model is a hard-top convertible Roadster manufactured by Mercedes Benz. 2 doors and 2 seats. Sold new in 2006. Fuel consumption of 12 liters/100km (Average). 0 to 100 km/h (62mph) in 4.2 seconds. A maximum top speed of 253 km/h. A curb weight of 1575 kgs. It has a naturally-aspirated 5.5 l V 8 hand-built “and signed” engine. This engine produces a maximum power of 355 bhp - 265 kW. The power is transmitted to the road by the rear wheel drive (RWD) with a 7 speed Automatic gearbox. For stopping power, the SLK (R171) 55 AMG braking system includes Vented Discs at the front and Vented Discs at the rear. It boasts an electrically controlled convertible hard-top, air scarf heated seats, factory fitted stereo. DVD player and 6 disc CD stacker. The vehicle currently has a low 82,000 km on the clock. Thank you for reading. Have a wonderful day! Shane.

description: THE STORY  A cultural icon of the 1980s, the Ferrari Testarossa was a two-door coupe that went into production in 1984 as the successor to the Ferrari Berlinetta Boxer. It was designed by Pininfarina in Italy and was produced from 1984 until 1991, with two model revisions (the 512 TR and F512 M) which were produced from 1992 until 1996. Including revised variations, almost 10,000 cars in total were made.    All versions of the Ferrari Testarossa came equipped with a rear-mounted 5-speed manual transmission and were built with a rear mid-engine design to keep the centre of gravity in the middle of the car. This was done to increase stability and improve cornering ability.    The Testarossa was powered by a 4.9L (301ci) flat 12-cylinder engine that produced 385HP. Top speed was 288kph with a 0-100kmph time of 4.8 seconds – extremely quick for the time.    The ‘Testarossa’ name pays homage to the famed 1957 World Sportscar Championship-winning 250 Testa Rossa sports racing car. Testarossa literally translates to “redhead” in Italian and refers to the car’s red-painted cam covers.    As well as being a poster car for a generation, the Testarossa also became a movie and TV star, featuring most notably in the 1980’s TV series, Miami Vice.    THE CAR  Originally delivered to Illinois and imported from North Carolina to Australia in 2023, this left-hand drive 1987 Ferrari Testarossa is in fantastic condition with low genuine mileage – only 30,193 miles on the odometer. This car has a clean Carfax History report that covers its time in the USA.    She is finished in gorgeous ‘Rosso Corsa’ red with a beautiful tan leather interior and factory tinted windows. It’s easy to see why this car was such an icon for the 1980s – every detail from the famed ‘cheese grater’ side intakes, the low hung stance and the high-mounted ‘flying wing’ mirrors gives the impression of aerodynamic performance.    The interior is excellent and equipped with a slew of features including an electronic glovebox, air-conditioning, an electronic ‘VegliaFlash Borletti’ digital clock, power windows and electronically adjustable seats. An aftermarket ‘Alpine’ head unit equipped with FM/AM radio and a CD player has been installed and tastefully concealed behind a leather cover on the dash. A remote control is included for the head unit.    The 4.9L (301ci) ‘Tipo’ F-113 flat-12 engine had its engine-out belt service and major service (including gearbox) in North Carolina on 26th April 2022. Both windows and all switches were also serviced.    Power is put to the road via the rear-mounted 5-speed manual transmission, and the car is equipped with a rear suspension system comprised of independent unequal length wishbones, coil springs, twin telescopic shock absorbers on each side and an anti-roll bar. This combined with the rear-center engine placement and the wide stance of the car ensure impeccable handling and sensational ride quality.    This vehicle comes with reproduction owner’s manuals and the original toolkits as well. The service history available is from the Carfax Vehicle History Report. The car comes with a Victorian Roadworthy Certificate from 2024. The Australian Import Approval is to hand.    There’s nothing quite like the famous roar of a 12-cylinder Ferrari Testarossa.

description: Mercedes' gorgeous two-seat convertible ruled the 1990s and is a new classic that's poised to significantly increase in value!    The R129-generation SL debuted for the 1990 model year to tremendous pent-up demand.    Its predecessor, the R107, had languished in production for 18 long years, and the new model was a quantum leap in design, engineering, safety, and performance.    Delayed nearly a decade while Mercedes focused on its new small sedans (the 190E and 300E), Bruno Sacco's R129 matured in the studio and emerged as a timeless, sophisticated, and impossibly elegant triumph of industrial design.    Better yet, the R129 was as much substance as style, with safety and technical innovations that were a decade or more ahead of most every other car on the road.    ABOUT THIS CAR        Beautiful colour...Beautiful overall condition.      Imported from Japan first registered in New Zealand in 1998.      This model was a baller's car when new and remains one now.      The electrically adjustable rear view mirror is a perfect example of how Mercedes was on top of the world in the early '90s.      This car has magnesium seat frames with integrated seatbelts and power headrests. T      The SL was designed to be future-proof. All the tech went to people who didn't appreciate it, because they were wealthy and old and bought it because every touch point was full of sophistication, mechanical and otherwise.      It's mind-blowing how inexpensive these cars are now given how expensive they once were...but not for long. There will soon enough come a time, where you wish you bought this car a few years earlier...and NOW is the time to get into these.      Comes with quite a few records - looks to be a well serviced vehicle.      Body is clean and straight and paint is very good.      Interior is in very good factory condition - everything seems to work as it should.      Beneath that automatic folding top, the car’s interior is a product of its time. An early climate control system and lower centre console designed to hold cassette tapes are just two of the touches that qualify the R129 as a classic today. Or a modern classic, we should say. Because, while it may still lack the allure of some of the earlier SL models, it’s also wildly more affordable.      Comes with good service history.      Comfort, interior, Performance, Value - everything in this car is 10 out of 10. This is without a doubt one of the best cars Mercedes ever built. One has to drive it to appreciate it, and to this day, remains quite the head turner.      Fabulous engine with a classic rumble and horsepower to snap your neck. Passing on the highway is a breeze and only requires a moderate level of nerve.      NOTE: This is not an AMG model.    If you had to pick one convertible to represent the 1990s, the SL500 would be the favorite based on its pop-culture profile alone.    It's all about the driving. And whether you pick the SL with its letters positioned after the number denoting the engine (1990-1993) or the SL with the letters positioned before the numbers (1994-2002), any well-maintained R129, like this one, should provide a dignified driving experience.    In fact, Princess Diana’s choice in motors is the most memorable among the royal family. In 1991, having tired of her stately Jaguar XJS, the People’s Princess traded it in for something new. Her choice sparked outcry, for it was the first time a British royal had not opted for a British car. What’s more, it was German. But we remain firm defenders of Di’s favoured wheels; the inimitable, unstoppable Mercedes-Benz R129 SL.    A sound investment, then, now and in future. description: 1982 FERRARI MONDIAL QV COUPE  SN: 4380   VIN: ZFFLD14C000044501    ENG:   F106A100551    $97,500  (To be sold Unregistered & with Vic RWC)    FOUR SEAT FERRARI       The Mondial (world car) was conceived as a 'usable' Ferrari when released, offering the practicality of four seats and the performance expected of a Ferrari. With Pinninfarina designed bodywork the Mondial was designed to provide rapid, luxurious transport for up to 4 people.    With the Quattrovalvole or QV, introduced in 1982, featured a new, 4 valve head, allegedly based on the early eighties Formula 1 engine and produced a respectable 240hp. When released the Mondial had a top speed of 230kmh and even today is still a desirable sports car from the world's greatest specialist manufacturer.     This Mondial was delivered to its first custodian on 21 January 1983 by Modena Station Garage in East Horsley, England before making its way to Hong Kong around 1989 where it remained until being imported to Australia in 2002, retained in the most recent ownership since late 2015.     In late 2016, the body benefited from a comprehensive restoration, with rust repair, and a bare metal repaint in Standox ‘Blu Chiaro’ completed by Classic Auto Refinishing of Bayswater Vic, while Ferrari specialist ‘Black Stallion’ of Ringwood Vic undertook the required disassembly and re-build.    A comprehensive history file, including original books as well as invoices dating back to 1990 accompanies the Mondial, with the most recent service completed by ‘Hughes Supercar Services’ of Braeside Victoria, in March 2025 at 59,629 miles, including: replacement of timing belts, engine & gearbox oil, coolant, an engine tune, replacement of the coolant expansion tank, a brake fluid flush & bleed and a Victorian Roadworthy Certificate sign off.       With a strong 3 litre V8, 5 speed manual gearbox, taut suspension and stainless steel Nouvalari exhaust it is a pleasure to drive. If your dream is a modern Italian classic with the practicality of 4 seats, performance and heritage, this Mondial could be for you. Chassis 889616 / Engine RA4524 - 9 / Body Number V7036 / Gearbox EB12715JS - Jaguar Heritage Certificate Available.      Restoration - this took place in the 90's and the car is still pretty much Mint. As one may see from photos, this car was completely stripped and rebuild. description: When someone asks if you'd like to drive their Jaguar E-Type, you say yes.    This car is like a celebrity. It burns itself into our collective consciousness on looks alone, but mechanically, it's equally wondrous. You feel like you know it, even if you don't. But just like you can't truly know someone only by reading their autobiography, you can’t know a car without driving it.    Semi-monocoque construction, stylish aerodynamics, innovative independent rear suspension, and disc brakes, all powered by one of the finest straight-six engines ever devised. The people who created the E-Type had developed machines that helped the Allies win World War II, not to mention earning Jaguar six Le Mans victories by 1957. This was the best British engineering of the time, wrapped up in an exceptionally gorgeous package.    The E-Type is derived from the D-Type, with influence from the XK-SS and the prototype entered by Briggs Cunningham at Le Mans in 1960.    Some alterations are technical improvements, while others have been introduced as an adaptation to series production.    In styling, no concessions have been given to current fashion, and the body is not the result of thorough wind-tunnel tests. Jaguar's chief aerodynamicist Malcolm Sayer created the body shape on a purely mathematical basis and actual experience has proved the car to have a very low drag.    ABOUT THIS CAR        Matching Numbers Car.      It was first registered in New Zealand from California USA in November 1995 with 43833 Miles.      First owner in New Zealand owned for 13 years who done 3379 miles in it. Second owner for 1 year who done circa 500 miles on it. Third owner for 10 years who done only 426 miles in it. Fourth owner was a customer of ours and done very little miles in it.      This car is beautiful to look at from any angle, and the pictures here fail to do the car justice.      The racing-type steering wheel, the large round instruments, the wire wheels, the bucket seats and the general low build of the car all contribute to give it a most businesslike air.      The responsiveness of the engine is eye-opening. The tach needle will rocket up to the red line and beyond with the engine showing no signs of stress in any speed range.      Engine noise is astounding - a very purposeful, comforting sound of well-­fitted parts doing their job right.      Overall Condition is Mint - body is straight and pretty much flawless. The paint is absolutely Stunning. The interior is spot on. The engine bay is clean and beautiful..      Comes with the right Dunlop tires on chrome wires.      To say this E-Type attracts interest wherever we go with it is a gross understatement. Men and women of all age and income groups come up and ask questions:  How fast will it go? How much does it cost? It is a great crowd drawer and a terrific ego booster, and if you want to get away from it all and go for that nice drive somewhere or weekend away, we can't think of a nicer car to do that in.    To the British motor industry, the name of Jaguar spells success: success on the most famous racing circuits in the world, and commercial success on every market where the make has been offered. What is the secret of this success? That question is probably best answered by the words of a well-known British ex-racing driver: ``Jaguar may not be the best car of its class in the world, but it is incontestably the least expensive of the MOST ICONIC CARS OF ALL TIME.``    When the E Type came out, it was expected to evolve and become one of the world's truly great cars from any standpoint and what a prophetic expectation that was.    A decent E-type is a joy on the open road, the long bonnet encouraging you to point and floor it. A 0-60 time of only 6.9 seconds is fast even by today's standards, let alone those of the 1960s. Proves every bit as good as it looks.    A STUNNING example, that will only appreciate in value. description:
The beautiful Alfa Romeo 105 coupe was immediately the darling of the cool car buyers when launched in the mid-1960s.

With specification including a lively twin-camshaft engine, 5-speed gearbox and disc brakes with gorgeous styling by Georgetto Giugaro at Bertone, the car was hard to resist. Today these cars are highly collectable and sought after by aficionados around the world.

This car was delivered new, by Paramotors in Perth and the first owner was a Mr Williams of Mt Lawley. The car always remained in Perth and by the 1990s was quite run down. The present owner bought the Alfa in 1996. He undertook a thorough restoration of the car, in which every element of the car was given attention – the result being a multi-award winner.

After a couple of years, the owner found he was using the car too infrequently and sold it. The new oner fitted a 2-litre motor. Unfortunately the car was damaged in Perth’s huge hailstorm of 2010 and repairs were begun, but not completed. The owner who’d previously restored the car bought it back and undertook a second restoration.

This took place from 2016 to 2020. The repaired bodywork was repainted, a new interior (from Alfaholics) was sourced, the gearbox rebuilt and a correct year 1600cc engine bought, completely rebuilt and fitted. Many parts specific to this model were sourced from overseas.

It is very evident from a close look that the car has been conscientiously restored and to a high standard. It has been to some club displays and on a few club runs when it’s performed faultlessly.

However the owner has found again that he’s making too little use of the car – he has several others… So it’s time to let it go to another enthusiast who will get more use and enjoyment out of the car.

With today’s restoration costs so high and lengthy waiting lists, this Alfa offers a ready-to-enjoy stylish classic which is a joy to drive and an absolute beauty to admire.

The plates UGT 105 will be retained by the owner.

title: 1971 jaguar e type v12 fhc automatic coupe

description:
MG built its post-war reputation with the T-series roadsters, which sold in record numbers. The small, nimble sports cars were great fun to drive.

This TF 1500 is understood to have been sold in Perth. The previous owner had it shipped the car to New South Wales when he moved there temporarily. Whilst in Sydney, some major work was undertaken on the car. He owned the car for 19 years.

The engine was completely rebuilt, and at the same time considerable other work undertaken. This included work on the electricals, new clutch, water pump, new hoses and a stainless steel exhaust system being fitted. A figure in excess of $20,000 was spent on this work, detailed in the car’s history file. This was carried out by a well-respected marque specialist.

In the ensuing years maintenance and minor work was undertaken.

The car changed hands in early 2023 and since then has had a few items attended to. The carburettors were sent to a leading expert company in Sydney and completely rebuilt (at a cost of some $2500). The dynamo and tachometer drive were rebuilt by a Perth MG specialist. The grease point for the rear of the dynamo and the tacho drive is for decorative purposes only. It is now a sealed bearing but the grease point is there reflecting the original. And lastly a number of gaskets were replaced to tackle some minor oil leaks. This most recent job in January 2025.

The car runs like a gem, the sporty exhaust note matching the car’s good performance.

The interior is very good with leather seats and the car has a cloth (not vinyl) soft top, side curtains and full tonneau, all in very good condition as can be seen in the accompanying photos.

About twenty years ago the MG was the subject of a body restoration, which has stood the test of time well. A couple of parts are showing some ageing and there are a couple of small marks in the paintwork, but generally, the car presents very nicely – see the photos.

This car would make a great fun car for weekend fun, or could equally be used in historic motorsport events. Parts availability is excellent and several car clubs cater enthusiastically for MGs.

description: THE STORY  Holding the title as Jaguar’s top-of-the-range saloon car from 1961 to 1970, the Jaguar Mark X was a hallmark car for Jaguar as it introduced radically different styling and technology from its predecessors.    The Mark X was the first Jaguar to feature an upright and often forward-facing front fascia and grille flanked by prominent quad round headlights.    Making its debut within a year of Jaguar’s iconic E-Type sportscar, the Mark X integrated much of the E-Type’s technology, innovations and specifications. The Mark X featured monocoque construction as well as power-assisted 4-wheel disc brakes and independent rear-suspension, which was unheard of for early 1960’s British luxury vehicles.    Originally fitted with a 3.8L triple-carbuettor in-line six-cylinder engine, an enlarged 4.2L variant fitted with triple ‘SU Carburretors’ became available for the London Motor Show in October of 1964.    Power-assisted steering came as standard across all Mark X’s, however the 4.2L variants received ‘Marles Varamatic Bendix (Adwest)’ variable ratio steering boxes, which were designed by an Australian, Arthur Bishop.    Of the Jaguar Mark X’s produced, the 4.2L variants are considered to be the rarest as only 5,137 were built, and it is unknown how many have survived the test of time.    A 4.2L Jaguar Mark X was famously owned and driven by Madonna.    THE CAR  Built in January of 1966 in Browns Lane, Coventry in the UK - this example of a Jaguar Mark X was Australian delivered to Adelaide SA in June of 1966. This car has had only 5 owners from new, with the current owner in possession of the vehicle for 7 years.    Finished in Opalescent Maroon which is in original (driver) condition, the car features a beige leather interior with a complimenting wood-grain trim. The inside is incredibly spacious with more than enough room to transport 5 people and their luggage in comfort.    Extensive mechanical work has been carried out on the vehicle over the years. The motor was rebuilt approximately 10 years ago. An aftermarket ‘Bell’ exhaust has been fitted and the fuel pump has been replaced. The front brakes were entirely rebuilt around 4 years ago, and the braking system and lines were also upgraded. New tyres were fitted at the same time, and 6 new shock absorbers have been fitted as well under current ownership.    The car is equipped with the desirable 4.2L six-cylinder engine fitted with triple ‘SU Carburettors’ mated to a 3-speed automatic transmission. Stopping power is handled by power-assisted four-wheel disc brakes, and the handling is excellent thanks to the inclusion of power-assisted steering and independent rear suspension.    An opportunity to own one of Jaguar’s most renowned and rare innovations.

description:
The Bentley Eight was introduced in 1984 as a more contemporary and accessible version of the Mulsanne, aimed at attracting a younger, more dynamic clientele to the revered British marque. With its upright mesh grille, minimalist badging, and restrained styling, the Eight retained all the gravitas expected of a Crewe-built car—yet presented it in a more understated and sporting manner. Built on Bentley’s traditional ladder-frame platform and powered by the iconic 6.75L V8 mated to a more reliable 3-speed automatic transmission, the Eight was a grand touring saloon in the purest sense: refined, unhurried, and immensely capable on long-distance journeys.

This model is often regarded as one of the most reliable of all Bentley saloons, thanks to its simpler, more robust engineering. It does not feature the later and more complex electronically-controlled suspension systems, making it a preferred choice among classic Bentley enthusiasts for its mechanical integrity and long-term maintainability. Its naturally-aspirated 6.75-litre V8 delivers turbine-like smoothness and ample low-end torque with effortless composure.

This magnificent example was built in late 1989 and complied in January 1990. It is one of the very few Bentley Eights delivered new in solid Black, a colour seldom seen on these cars and perfectly paired with a Mushroom leather interior accented by high-gloss Piano wood trim throughout the cabin. It was delivered new by Hamilton’s Rolls-Royce & Bentley of Richmond, the premier Bentley dealer in Victoria, and has travelled just 154,099km from new.

Adding a tasteful and eye-catching twist to its already striking presentation, this Bentley has been rebadged with deep red Bentley 'B' emblems in place of the standard black items, complemented by matching deep red coachline pinstripes. As there is no red version of the original Eight badge, a Turbo R badge has been fitted to the boot lid purely to complete the look—though the car remains an original, naturally-aspirated Eight. description: With the factory fitted twin SU carburettors, the engine developed 140 horsepower and the Daimler could reach nearly 180 kph, performance which was accompanied by a lovely V8 exhaust note through the twin pipes. Most Daimler 2.5 V8s also came with Borg-Warner's excellent T35 automatic transmission that worked well with the engine's characteristics. The Daimler 2.5 V8 had a warm, traditional ambience with a walnut veneer dashboard with full instrumentation, an adjustable split bench front seat, lush carpets, and West of England headlining. This Daimler came with leather upholstery. Looking at it dispassionately, you would logically buy a Daimler 2.5 V8 saloon over its Jaguar Mk2 stablemate. After all, the Daimler boasted a V8 engine compared to the Jaguar’s 2.4/3.4/3.8 straight six, was finished to higher level of luxury, and there were far fewer made, less than 18,000 in the case of the Daimler compared to almost 84,000 Jaguars. That has made the Daimler great value in the classic car market, especially with good examples around, such as this 1964 car. Bought from an official of the Daimler & Landcaster Club in early 2016 by the previous owner, the 2.5 V8 saloon was the recipient of an Opalescent Silver Grey paintwork refresh in the 1990s and is now showing a few blemishes of age. There are some very minor blistering and cracks evident. Inside, our Daimler is finished in grey leather which remains in good condition, as does the extensive woodwork, while the original radio works, sadly the clock doesn’t. There’s a complete original tool kit in the boot, which is neatly carpeted and comes with the jack. Under the shapely bonnet, the 2.5 litre V8 has a non-original aftermarket alloy radiator, along with a manually activated thermatic fan, Bosch electronic ignition, and a new battery was fitted recently. Recent work has included adding a second (electric) fuel pump, new hoses in the engine bay, and a generator rebuild. This Daimler also comes with an enormous amount of supportive paperwork, much of it from its previous Club member owner. There’s a folder containing its service history with numerous receipts, another one with original paperwork – including the Owner’s manual – showing its factory order and subsequent shipping to Australia. There’s also a Lucas parts catalogue. Another folder contains a plethora of reference materials including relevant magazine technical articles, plus the dedicated clubman’s personal notes and tips. And finally, there’s a trio of factory Maintenance handbooks, a Daimler Service manual, a Daimler Parts catalogue, and several other official publications. Winner of the Best Car 1960 – 1970 award at the 2014 Daimler & Lancaster Club National Rally, this ’64 2.5 V8 saloon presents possibilities for the keen enthusiast. It would be simple to using it as a daily driver, or on special club events. This car is an absolute gem to drive and will not disappoint a genuine buyer. Currently on non-transferable club registration. LVD3382
