description:
Chicane Auctions is proud to present this beautifully preserved and highly desirable 1974 Porsche 911 S Coupe, an Australian-delivered, matching-numbers example offered with a complete service history from new and an outstanding record of care spanning five decades.

MODEL OVERVIEW
The 1974 Porsche 911 S is a standout from the early G-series era, blending classic long-hood charm with mechanical updates.

At its heart is a free-revving 2.7-litre air-cooled flat-six engine, derived from the legendary 1973 Carrera RS. In S specification, it produced 175 horsepower (130 kW) and 235 Nm of torque, channeled through a crisp-shifting 5-speed manual gearbox or the optional Type 925 Sportomatic transmission.

With a kerb weight just over 1,070kg, the 911 S could sprint from 0–100 km/h in around 6.5 seconds—brisk for its time—and topped out near 225 km/h.

Fitted with distinctive chrome trim, 15-inch cast aluminium ATS wheels and elegant body shape, the '74 911 S strikes a perfect balance of classic style and usability.

The handling remained sharp thanks to its low weight, torsion bar suspension and near 40:60 weight distribution.

Legendary Porsche ventilated disc brakes at all four corners for always dependable stopping power.

It’s the kind of Porsche that rewards spirited driving, turns heads, and delivers a visceral connection that’s made it a cult favourite among purists —light, responsive, and beautifully simple.  

DRIVELINE
This 911 S retains its original matching-numbers 2.7-litre flat-six engine, now tastefully upgraded with triple-throat Weber 40 IDA carburettors—a popular period-correct performance modification inspired by the legendary Carrera RS.

The engine has been professionally rebuilt and delivers strong, responsive power. A stainless steel exhaust system adds a purposeful tone and complements the upgrades beautifully.

Power is delivered through the standard Type 915 five-speed manual gearbox, known for its direct mechanical feel. This is a well-balanced, driver-focused 911 that remains true to its roots while delivering enhanced performance.

EXTERIOR
Presented in its factory Code 117 Light Yellow, this 911 S has an honest, appealing patina that reflects decades of care rather than restoration.

The body presents straight and true, with factory-correct chrome window trims, headlamp rings, and exterior mirrors, as fitted to the 911 S variant. Period-correct 15-inch cast aluminium ATS wheels remain fitted, adding further distinction and originality to the car’s visual appeal.

INTERIOR
The interior remains mostly faithful to factory specification, with original finishes in remarkably well-preserved condition. The classic five-gauge Porsche dashboard layout, deep bolstered seats and Nardi steering wheel combine to create a cockpit built for driving.

Subtle period-correct details throughout reaffirm this car’s authenticity. It’s an inviting space that rewards both weekend use and spirited drives alike.

SUMMARY
Today, the 1974 Porsche 911 S occupies a unique place in the 911 timeline. It bridges the gap between the raw, pre-impact-bumper cars of the late 1960s and the more refined but heavier SC and Carrera 3.2 models of the 1980s.

It still feels light, responsive, and mechanical—everything that makes a vintage 911 special—yet benefits from improved safety, usability, and drivability.

Its direct link to the Carrera RS, low production numbers (especially for right-hand drive and Australian delivery), and enduring classic looks make it an increasingly appealing proposition for both driving enthusiasts and savvy collectors.

Offered with a fully documented service history from new, this example benefits from long-term ownership and careful stewardship throughout its life.

A classic air-cooled 911 that is more fun driving at 80 kph, than a modern version at 200 kph.

The Auction will be held Online, ensuring collectors across Australia have equal opportunity to bid and own.

AUCTION CLOSES: MAY 15th from 8:30pm (AEST).

description: The elegant Rolls-Royce Silver Cloud enjoyed a decade long production run at Crewe, replacing the Silver Dawn in 1955. Based on an entirely new chassis, the Cloud featured independent front suspension and semi-elliptic rear springs to give superb roadholding and ride characteristics. Adjustable rear shock absorbers (via a switch on the steering column) were a novel feature, while hydraulically operated brakes ensured excellent stopping power, and power steering became a standard feature shortly after the model’s introduction. Although the Cloud initially retained the Silver Dawn’s six-cylinder engine, the motor’s capacity was raised to 4.9-litres and power was transmitted via a new four-speed automatic transmission, developed by General Motors and built under licence. Styled by John Blatchley and Ivan Evernden, the Cloud’s standard steel coachwork has a graceful beauty that has withstood the test of time. The interior was superbly appointed, with Connolly leather upholstery, and timber facia, door cappings and rear picnic tables. Although the original Silver Cloud sold in good numbers, Rolls-Royce was already developing a new engine worthy of the car, a 6.2 litre light alloy V8. The new unit was both smoother and more powerful than the in-line six it replaced and went on to power every car to wear the famous Flying Lady for the next 40 odd years. The V8-engined Silver Cloud II was visually indistinguishable from its six-cylinder predecessor, but just three years later Rolls-Royce updated the styling, adding twin headlamps either side of a revised radiator shell, plus combined sidelamp/indicators, to create the Cloud III model. The front and rear seats were also redesigned (separate front seats were now standard), while changes to the carburettors and a higher compression ratio raised the power output as well. Rolls-Royce built just 2555 Silver Cloud IIIs (with a further 1286 Bentley S3 variants) between 1962 and 1965, of which the vast majority were fitted with standard coachwork, although a small number received bespoke bodywork from the likes of H J Mulliner. A further 254 long-wheelbase Cloud IIIs were also produced.

description: Last of the E-Type family that's more GT than sports car.    The Series 3 is the best sorted of them all, as well as the cheapest way to buy this legendary big cat because while the earlier cars still carry a significant premium, the Series 3 is the most usable E-type of them all.    When Jaguar unveiled the third iteration of its E-type in 1971 there were sharp intakes of breath. Here was a car with a wheelbase stretched by nine inches compared with its predecessor, so its cabin was as spacious as an E-type 2+2’s, things improved a little further by the car’s width increasing by an inch. Power came from an engine with twice as many cylinders as before.    Compared with the six-cylinder editions that went before, the S3 is a completely different animal with its V12 engine.    Its bigger and more spacious than its predecessors while also being much more relaxed to drive. But it’s certainly no slouch as it can go from 0-60mph in just 6.4 seconds and it tops out at 142mph, so there’s no shortage of urge.    ABOUT THIS CAR        Chassis#: 1S50866      FHC 2+2      VERY GOOD Condition and very well maintained - one of the best we've had...      Good provenance - comes with a very comprehensive file demonstrating maintenance history, and upkeep.      Today, the car is best described as an older restoration that is still in beautiful condition.      Brand new hood-lining.      Factory RHD - this car was imported from South Africa and was first registered in New Zealand in 1999.      One owner in New Zealand for the last 24 years.      Beautiful grand tourer - an absolute delight to drive especially with 4 speed Manual transmission.      Power Steering.      Mechanically sound - awesome to drive and comes with the most beautiful note      Comes complete with spare wheel, jack, tools and lots of books and lots of other facory records.      STUNNING CAR!    VALUES - The ceiling for these cars nowadays is generally around NZD200K, although the odd exceptional car might change hands for a bit more – potentially as much as NZD235K.    Some are advertised for more than this but whether or not they sell is a moot point. At this level such cars are really aimed at collectors who are unlikely to use their cars; they’ll be completely restored; best of the best examples. Quite a few Series 3 owners do use their Jaguars a fair bit for touring, and to buy something suitable you should expect to spend somewhere between NZD185K and NZD200K for a really nice 2+2.    E-types are still coming back from the US, but these are more often six-cylinder cars rather than V12s. Obviously, they’ll be in left-hand drive form and such cars will always be worth less in NZ unless they’re converted to right-hand drive.    It’s taken a long time but the market has now latched on to the fact that the S3 is a great car.    However, part of the reason for the increase in values is they’ve been dragged up by the earlier cars becoming so expensive to buy that enthusiasts can no longer afford them, so they’re turning to the V12 models instead. That makes the S3 sound like the poor relation, but the V12-powered E-type is no consolation price, as it’s the most usable of the breed. Its also the most highly developed.    For a long time many E-type fans bought a V12 because they couldn’t afford anything else, but the cat is now out of the bag and classic car fans are appreciating this E-type in its own right.    With great specialist and club support, the S3 makes huge sense on many levels; these cars are surprisingly usable, even on the longest journeys.    FINANCE AVAILABLE! description: 1962 AUSTIN HEALEY 3000 MkII  SN: 4356   REG:266XPR   VIN:HBT7L17726   ENG:29E RUH/4056    $115,000  (To be sold Unregistered & with Vic RWC)    LAST OF THE ROADSTERS, LOVINGLY RESTORED    Introduced in May of 1961 the 3000 MkII was the final Healey Roadster, featuring the same bodywork, suspension and running gear as the 3000 MkI, with the exception of a new vertical grill, and triple 1½” SU Carburettors. Power was increased to 132bhp, but most importantly allowed the works teams to homologate triple carburettors (DCOE45 Webers) on their rally cars. Six months into production, in November of 1961 the new 'Centre Shift' gearbox was introduced to the 3000 MkII, creating the “Last and Best” Austin Healey Roadster produced.    Delivered new to Portland Oregon, this BT7 drove off the production line in late January 1962, finished in Healey Blue with blue trim, optioned with wire wheels, Overdrive, a heater and an adjustable steering column.    Imported into Australia in 1988, this 3000 MkII was then sold to a Tasmanian enthusiast who in May 1990 commissioned The Healey Factory to undertake the required full restoration. Stripped to a bare metal shell, and rebuilt from the ground up, the restoration took 15 months, with the Healey Roadworthy, Engineered and Registered in August 1991.    Subsequent owners have lovingly cared for the MkII, with a number of reliability upgrades taking place between 2011 and 2013, including the fitment of: enlarged, triple 1¾” SU carburettors, twin fuel pumps, electronic ignition, a spin on oil filter conversion, an alternator and a hi-torque starter motor.    Supported by a large file of receipts, documenting the restoration, upgrades and maintenance work carried out, this BT7 is ready for a new home, begging to have it’s legs stretched on open country roads. description: The Rolls-Royce Twenty built between 1922 and 1929 was Rolls-Royce's ``small car`` for the 1920s and was produced alongside the 40/50 Silver Ghost and the successor to the 40/50, the Phantom.    Quickly nicknamed the Baby Rolls Royce, it was designed to allow the company’s customers to drive their own cars, particularly in city traffic, where the compact car was certainly more at ease than the huge Silver Ghost cars.    It was truly the first production Rolls Royce compact car and was also perfectly suited to long journeys.    The first generations of the Twenty are identifiable by the radiator flaps being placed horizontally rather than vertically, as was then the norm at Rolls Royce.    As for the engine, although the brand remained faithful to the six-cylinder engine, it decided to study a new engine, the first with overhead valves, with a displacement of 3,127 cm3, consisting of a single cylinder block with a detachable cylinder head and a single ignition.    The chassis was shorter than traditional Rolls Royce cars and had rigid front and rear axles suspended by semi-elliptical springs.    Braking on this model was provided only on the rear wheels before the introduction of drum brakes with mechanical servo on all four wheels in 1925. The Twenty was later equipped with hydraulic shock absorbers.    The driver, not the chauffeur anymore, has a three-speed gearbox with the gear change initially placed in the centre of the passenger compartment, before being replaced in 1925 by a four-speed gearbox with the traditional gear change to the right of the driver. The driver could expect to reach a maximum speed of 97 km/h.    As was customary at the time, Rolls Royce manufactured only the chassis and mechanics of the Twenty. Indeed, customers had the choice of commissioning the UK’s most famous coachbuilders to build a dedicated body. At the time, the big names were Barker, Park Ward, Thrupp & Maberly, Mulliner, Hopper, Kellner and Gurney Nutting.    The Twenty was produced in 2,940 units between 1922 and 1929. It became a mainstay of the company and was replaced by the 20/25 and then the 25/30 4.3 litre in 1936.    ABOUT THIS CAR        Chassis#: GF41      Engine: G693      Original Certificate Of Registration Available      NZ New - First Owner HW White      This car is in very nice condition with just the right amount of patina. Its truly beautiful inside out.      4-door saloon body type      RWD (rear-wheel drive), manual 3-speed gearbox      Characteristic dimensions: outside length: 4521 mm / 178 in, width: mm / in, wheelbase: 3277 mm / 129 in      Top speed: 105 km/h (65 mph) (declared by factory)    Aimed at the professional segment of the middle-class owner-drivers such as doctors, dentists, solicitors and moderately successful businessmen, the Twenty cost about 40% less than a Ghost, yet still met the same exacting standards of design, materials and workmanship.    In the year of its launch in 1922, it had a chassis price of 1,100 (pounds). The Twenty was conceived and executed with typical attention to detail, object, being as stated by Royce: 'to spend as much money in the construction as can be done wisely, but not unnecessarily'.    The Twenty had been built to carry open and enclosed bodies with up to six seats, but with a light body it was capable of what Royce called a high road speed. In 1922 40 mph was considered a fast cruising speed, yet the Twenty was capable of just over 60 mph.    Ongoing development of the car, a process the company used on most models, eventually upped the top speed to over 70 mph.    Henry Royce's biographer, Sir Max Pemberton, raved about his Twenty. 'The late Lord Northcliffe once said to me that as an instrument of advertising British efficiency in industry, the Rolls-Royce car was unique. When I reflect upon the performance of the 'Twenty' I have driven now for six years, I am wholly in accord with this opinion. It is surely one of the world's two great cars. The other is the 'Phantom'.    SHIPPING CAN BE ARRANGED FOR OUR OVERSEAS CLIENTS & TRANSPORT THROUGHOUT NEW ZEALAND CAN BE ORGANISED ON BUYER'S BEHALF. description: Delivered new to North Brede Motors in Perth and sold to Peter Alexander Bell from Bassendean WA, in November 1967, this Alfa Romeo 2600 Sprint presents in its original Bianco Antico with black leather interior. It is a lovely driver’s car which has been well looked after by the current owner for 20 years.  It is a 4-owner car and comes with its original service books and keys.   The 2600 Sprint really defined the executive driver’s car for Alfa Romeo. Built between 1964 and 1967 only 6,999 were made and of those a mere 597 were RHD of which our car is one of these.  This larger grand touring coupé could seat four adults in comfort over long journeys at high speeds thanks to the wide power and torque band of the 2584cc six-cylinder engine. With a 5 speed gearbox and all round disc brakes it was perfect to drive long distances at speed and in comfort.  The design is the result of Giorgetto Giugiaro's first major project as head designer for Carrozzeria Bertone, and is arguably one of the most influential designs in the history of automotive styling.    Of the 597 RHD cars, very few were sold new in Australia and this is one of those. Its VIN starting in 854 confirms this was a produced for the Australian market and is underlined in the original sales documents which accompany the car.  The body of the car is in very good condition and the colour of the paint suits the car setting off the brightwork well. The car has had a recent full body repaint which is of good quality. There is no evidence of rust anywhere on the car and it suggests it has clearly lead a pampered life.  The engine and gearbox both perform faultlessly with no issues with the synchro’s. Over the last few years the car has been driven on fair weather days and to ensure it drives well with recent mechanical work done to ensure it runs as expected.  The interior is very good and the leather has been replaced at some point but shows no signs of cracking or loss of colour, unusually the dash and steering wheel is sound without cracking too. The electric windows are in working correctly and the headlining is in superb order and the window chrome is spot on. The interior of this car really is a lovely place to be. The original radio blanking plate accompanies the car too highlighting how original this is.   The wheels although not original suit the car well. At some point the ‘2600’ badges and grill have been painted black as have the windscreen wipers, however these can be easily returned to standard.  Out on the road this car really is a gentlemen’s express and is incredibly quiet and comfortable to drive as it works through the gears with the 2.6 litre engine providing plenty of ‘go’ whilst delivering an intoxicating engine note.  Compared to its contemporaries from Maserati and Ferrari this represents something of a bargain and particularly one that is so original. A wonderful driving Alfa Romeo with a fantastic history.

description: 1962 PORSCHE 356 BT6 SUPER 90 SN: 4367 VIN: 120343 ENG: P805305 $275,000 (To be sold Unregistered & with Vic RWC) HAMILTONS DELIVERED MATCHING NUMBERS COUPE The 356 was Porsche's first production automobile and was the foundation vehicle for the iconic 911. Designed by Ferdinand ‘Ferry’ Porsche, it was a lightweight and nimble handling, rear-engine, rear-wheel-drive 2 door sports car available in hardtop or convertible configurations. This 356 from 1962 was delivered new by Hamiltons of South Yarra, one of very few that were delivered new to Australia, making it an extremely rare example. This Super 90 coupe in the updated T6 body type features twin grilles on the engine cover, larger windows, a handle on the ‘frunk’ tapered towards the bottom with the Porsche crest, headlights positioned higher up and teardrop shape taillights with integrated indicators. The Super 90 was factory rated at 90 horsepower from the Type 616/7 Boxer engine, a 50% improvement from a base 356 due to the increased 9.0:1 compression, stronger valve springs and uprated crankshaft with 55mm main bearings. The 356B presents in stunning condition, having received a bare metal repaint in 2013 in its factory original colour of Smyrna green, highlighted with stunning Brightwork and features a restored interior with black leather trim, period radio, inertia seat-belts and air conditioning. Mechanical improvements that benefit the 356 include a front disc brake conversion, Koni shock absorbers, Twin IDF40 Weber carburettors, 12 volt solenoid, starter and wiper motor. This 356 has been well maintained with a thick history file dating back to 2005, the most recent service was carried out by Beachside Automotive Services in April 2024. This award winning rare right hand drive 356B, complete with certificate of authenticity, has received multiple trophies from the annual Melbourne Porsche 356 parades. Priced without Reg, Talk to us about Reg, Club or Other Plate Options. description: THE STORY  Manufactured between 1954 and 1957, the Jaguar XK140 was the successor to the XK120. This beautiful sports car came with several upgrades, including improved brakes, more interior space, rack and pinion steering, increased suspension travel and telescopic shock absorbers instead of the older lever arm design.    In addition to these upgrades, the exterior of the car also received some changes, such as more substantial front and rear bumpers with overriders, and flashing turn signals above the front bumper, which could be activated by a switch on the dashboard. A chrome trim strip was added along the centre of the bonnet and boot lid, and an emblem on the boot lid contained the words “Winner Le Mans 1951-3”.    Powered by a 3.4L (207ci) Jaquar XK double-overhead camshaft inline-6 engine with Special Equipment modifications from the XK120, the XK140 was capable of outputting 190 bhp at 5,500 rpm as standard. An optional C-Type cylinder head pushed the performance even higher, producing 210 bhp at 5,750 rpm.    In 1956 the XK140 became the first Jaguar sports car to be offered with automatic transmission.    In total only 8,937 XK140s were ever built, making it an incredibly rare and sought after vehicle.    THE CAR  Purchased in 1999 by the current owner, this fantastic example of a 1957 Jaguar XK140 was lovingly and fully restored by the legendary late Gavin Sandford-Morgan at the V.M. Engineering Company over a four year period between 1999-2002. Originally a left-hand drive vehicle, it was professionally converted into right-hand drive during the restoration.    No expense was spared in bringing this car to life, and extensive records of the work carried out are supplied with purchase.    Finished in gorgeous Indigo Blue and with gleaming chrome work, this Jaguar is in fantastic condition inside and out and is sure to impress.    On the inside, the Grey Leather trim complements the accompanying blue carpet beautifully and looks sensational paired with the polished wood-grain dash, steering wheel and door edges. All instrumentation and electronics are in working order, and an aftermarket Kenwood head unit has been installed as well.    An extremely tight package, this car handles beautifully, boasts excellent power with the inline-6 engine and has a wonderful exhaust note. She is badged as a ‘Jaguar Type C’ indicating the presence of the optional C-Type cylinder head with more performance. The brakes have recently been overhauled, and the car has been equipped with an electric fuel-pump and a hard-wired trickle charger.    A soft car cover is included with the vehicle.    An excellent example of a rare and timeless classic – currently on historic registration in SA.

description: The SS was presented as a car for a motorist of discernment - a car for the discriminating - the keenly critical!    In a stereotyped age, the SS stood alone boldly individualistic - daring to be different.    At a time when mere cheapness was frequently of greater account then worth, the SS note of quality was insistent; while affinity between appearance and performance tended to become less, the SS offered both - in full measure.    It was for the experienced motorist that the SS held the most obvious appeal - the motorist who could appreciate the fine surge of power that answered his or her demand of acceleration...the effortless control at speeds in the 70's and 80's (mph)...the total lack of fatigue after long journeys at high speeds.    ABOUT THIS CAR        In the late 1960's, when collectors were gathering up early SS cars, the focus then was on the more glamorous six-cylinder models, and prices escalated dramatically, this little four cylinder was overlooked and considered to be the poor relation of the marque. Time has proved that this model is now considered to be among the most desirable types because of the more balanced contours of the design, and its rarity. Our research indicates that only about a dozen of these are known to have survived, and it is believed that this is the only one in the Southern Hemisphere with the others being in Europe and the USA.      When purchased by the last owner, back in 1968, the car had by then had at least 40 owners in NZ since its import in 1939. It was then in very poor condition with much modified bodywork, damaged chassis, incorrect instruments and an engine that was beyond repair.      A complete strip down revealed that this was not going to be an easy task and the project mothballed. It wasn't until circa 1985, that a serious attempt at reconstruction was started.      With the chassis realigned, body frame work renewed, and an uprated engine installed, it all started coming together as a viable project.      The many hours spent resulted in a car that is true to the original concept and it has proved to be road worthy and reliable ever since.      Some modifications should be noted here, as follows:- While the chassis and the running gear are strictly original, the old 10hp engine has been replaced with a later model Standard 14hp block. This has been over bored to 1820cc but has all the original 10hp accessories bolted to it except for carburetion. The engine is now fitted with twin SU carburettors (type D3) with a simple engine breathing system and has an harmonic balancer attached to the front pulley. the reason for these modifications is to extend the usable RPM range from 35600rpm to 4500rpm. Also the rear axle ratio has been changed to make use of the pulling power of the larger capacity engine.      The Vehicle still retains the original braking system, which is cable operated.      Twelve Volt battery      Distributor Lucas DKH4.0 Type V49      Tire Size 475/500-18 Goodrich      Runs best on 95 octane      First Registered in NZ on the 17th of January 1939      Leather grained trunk, with heavily chromium plated hinged security catches and ample accommodation.      Rigidly secured draughtproof side curtains that can be erected independently of the hood.    Concours History        1st place South Canterbury Vintage Car Club class 5th March 2000 Concours (first outing)      3rd equal place National Jaguar Rally Queenstown (2000) Early SS or Jaguar Concours      1st place SCVCC PV/PWV/P60V rally (2009) Concours    No matter in which direction personal taste inclined - closed car or open car - SS offered to the discriminating motorist something out of the ordinary...true individuality in performance and appearance. description: The Daimler V8 was the result of a lengthy plan to give Daimler a presence in the executive car sector as well as the luxury sector.    The first attempt to bridge this gap was a joint venture with Vauxhall, which would have led to a restyled PA Cresta with a Daimler V8 and trim. The Jaguar buyout of 1960 put paid to this, and in 1962 the 2.5 V8 saloon was created.    The Turner engine gives the whole car a very different, more louche feel than the sporting Jaguars, and as such appealed to different customers when new and on the classic market.    Daimler’s small 2.5 V8, was designed by Edward Turner of Triumph motorbike fame. Inspired in part by the contemporary Cadillac V8, he incorporated many of the design features seen in his motorbike engines; including hemispherical combustion chambers and push rods, with an overhead valve layout. Developing 140bhp, this engine was also used in the Daimler SP250 sports car – and is the reason the Daimler is seen as a separate entity to the Jaguars.    ABOUT THIS CAR        Chassis #: 1A8410BW      Engine #: 7A 8344      NZ NEW      Power steering      Body seems honest and clean of rust.      Chrome is in good condition.      Upholstery and door cards are factory original and in good condition.      Carpets, hood lining, sun visors, wind lace and rear shelf all in good order. (Note: passenger side carpet needs small repair, that will be done as part of the sale).      Wood in nice order.      Windscreen and door rubbers in good condition.      Comes complete with factory tool box, Jack and spare wheel      Mechanically sound car - runs and drives great - one of the nicest Daimler V8's we've driven.      This is a beautiful car in good overall condition - presented in the best color of them all - British racing Green :)      Sounds like a V8 should :)      Odometer in Miles    Whilst prices for good Jags spiral ever higher, one can burble along in a Daimler V8 feeling just as pleased about life, but at a fraction of the cost.    The trim level is higher than the MK2, too – when the 240 and 340 received Ambla trim, the Daimler V8-250 was never subjected to such indignities. They might not be as sporting – but let’s be honest, few MK2s are ever really driven in anger any more.    A beautiful Classic, that is ready to be enjoyed. description: Up for sale is my 1989/1990 FSM Niki 650. Vehicle is unregistered and will need to be transported on a tow truck/flatbed. It has a fully running engine and transmission however foot brake doesn't operate only the handbrake (master cylinder seized). Bought this originally to restore back to its former glory or modify in to a historic race car. Recommend for someone who if they want to restore it can repair rust and panels as there is a fair amount (see black taped areas on photos) but the worst part of all is the left/nearside A - pillar and windscreen area which has rusted through and would need a complete rebuild. This Niki still has many usable parts left on it, the engine is fully running and transmission/clutch also function. The gear selector rod bushing has perished so it requires a bit of playing around to get in to gear with the gearstick. A refurbished fuel pump was fitted years ago along with the starter motor being rebuilt. Even the alternator still provides charge at 13.8V. A Speeder sports muffler has been fitted as the original was rusted through, the ignition coil was replaced with a Mitsubishi coil. Car will be sold is as in the pictures. Will sell it with a brand new 430CCA Lion battery, only bought it so I can start the car to move around the backyard. It's the wrong sized battery for this car (suitable for e.g. Toyota Corolla, large battery posts) and has no battery hold down clamp but is enough to get the engine going.

description: THE STORY  Unveiled in 1985, the Mercedes-Benz 420 SEL was part of the renowned W126 series of full-size luxury sedans which would go on to become one of Mercedes-Benz most successful and iconic lines. The 420 SEL model debuted as a more luxurious and powerful option within the W126 range, offering superior performance, comfort and technology.    Visually, the 420 SEL featured the characteristic luxury and elegance of the W126 series, with its long, sleek body profile and subtle design touches. Inside, the cabin offered a refined and opulent atmosphere, with leather upholstery, wood trim, and high-quality materials throughout. The car was also equipped with a host of amenities, including power-adjustable seats, an advanced climate control system, and an innovative onboard electronics system for the time.    In terms of safety, the W126 series set a new benchmark with innovations such as anti-lock brakes (ABS), airbags, and a reinforced safety cell. The 420 SEL embodied the pinnacle of Mercedes-Benz's commitment to both engineering excellence and luxurious comfort, maintaining a reputation that has lasted for decades.    THE CAR  Australian delivered new to Pymble, New South Wales on the 30th of June in 1988 by Morrison Motors Pty Ltd, this 1988 Mercedes-Benz 420 SEL presents in Nautical Blue with a complementing trim in grey leather.    Believed to be a three-owner car from new, she still has her original delivery books, build sheet and the original sales brochure printed in German. Also accompanying this vehicle is a full service history and the original medical kit which is fully intact.    The 4.2L (256ci) V8 M116 engine delivers a robust 201 horsepower, and paired with the smooth 4-speed automatic transmission it offers refined performance, making this 420 SEL an excellent choice for long-distance cruising.    Features include power seats, power windows, power steering, powered sunroof, cruise control, functional climate control, powered side mirrors, working headlight wipers, replacement Pioneer sound system and AMG styled alloy wheels.    The wood grain is dark and in excellent condition as are the seats, carpet, headlining, door cards and dash. This is the long wheelbase version and there are original foot rests in the rear for additional passenger comfort.    Over the course of its life, this vehicle has required minimal work. The battery and fuel accumulator have been replaced, and the air-conditioner has been re-gassed.    This car is in immaculate condition for its age and shows only 103,912 kms on the clock. Currently on historic registration in SA.

description: The Jaguar MK VII - the First Jaguar Saloon to use a Twin OHC Engine.    Good to drive, big and comfortable Jaguar saloon that doesn't have too much of the 'spiv' image that would be associated with later saloons. Fast too if tuned, and misunderstood by anyone who has not driven one.    During the 1950s, Jaguar might have been wooing the world's sports car drivers with its XK120, but the big and imposing saloons coming out of Browns Lane were also winning friends, and selling well. Its post-war run of desirable and capable large saloons started modestly with the 2.5 Litre, but was was truly kickstarted with the arrival of the Mk7 in 1950.    Although similar under the skin to the outgoing car, the newer Mk7’s swooping styling with daring roof line and feline rear haunches was a huge leap forward visually, The Mk7 also saw the introduction of the twin-cam XK engine (first seen in the XK120) in a four-door for the first time, making it a genuine 100mph proposition and are well capable of being turned into fast and capable historic race cars.    SPECIFICATIONS        Six Cylinder Twin cam In Line 3442cc with Twin 1.75in SU Carburettors      Max Power 160bhp at 5200rpm      Manual 4 speed box      Front independent suspension Rear live axle, half-elliptic leaf springs      Burman Douglas Steering recirculating ball worm and nut      Hydraulic servo assisted brakes    OWNERSHIP HISTORY        Three long term owners on record - 6 years / 22 years / 10 years (with what looks to be some traders in between).    ABOUT THIS CAR        Body is straight, and from what we can see, seems to be clean from rust.      Good paintwork      Tidy upholstery - Seats and Door cards in good order / Carpets tidy and look original / Wood in good condition / hood-lining in good order.      This car comes with a lot of mechanical records dating back to 2010. It has had a real lot done to it and is a well sorted car.      Comes with Sunroof, Original jack and an original toolbox that we recently sourced for it. (Toolbox will need a tidy up).    These are really nice cars to drive. By putting the XK engine under the bonnet of the Mark VII, Jaguar pioneered the very idea of a saloon that could hold its own against dedicated sports cars. In fact, even as Jaguar was building its reputation with the C-type and D-type, dominating the 24 Hours of Le Mans during the mid-Fifties, Jaguar entered the Mark VII into other competitions, finding victory in the 1956 Monte Carlo Rally.    Everyone wants an XK120 or 140 or 150, but the more I look at the Mark VII, there just seem to be fewer of them out there and it's just a beautiful old car. It's the kind of car when you walk out and see it, it just brings a smile to your face.  I think it has a real, physical presence plus it's a piece of automotive history and it's one that you can still enjoy on today's roads. We absolutely love this car.    A Very Tidy example, that can only appreciate in value. description: Bentley is a marque associated with the utmost level of luxury, even if the archetypal Bentley was a fire-breathing, smoke-belching beast that left its well-heeled drivers' leather helmets and goggles covered in the debris of combustion and defeated rivals in its wake.    Races were won. Hills were conquered. Even decades after the marque's takeover by former rival Rolls-Royce, the performance heritage of Bentley remained unquestioned.    It makes sense that the Bentley Brooklands' very name conjures up racing and endurance record heritage, referring to the first-purpose built motor racing course that didn't begin life as a horse race track.    The sibling of the Rolls-Royce Silver Spirit/Spur II, the Brooklands succeeded the Eight and the Mulsanne, whose moniker also refers to a straight on a racing circuit, though in France.    The Brooklands and all Bentleys carry on with racing tradition.    Though the original Bentley Boys may have quite fancied danger along with a face full of exhausted long chain hydrocarbons, Bentley automobiles evolved with demands of absolute top appointments.    ABOUT THIS CAR    Imported from Singapore, this car was first registered in New Zealand in April 2001. It is in beautiful order and everything in it seems to work as it should.  This Brooklands, is certainly unique being originally destined for Singapore. It had many of the options ticked at the time, with some interesting non-standard features in the interior.  Singapore is a market whereby the majority of cars are built to a customer order.    This Bentley is a hand-built car. Many hands and many more hours were required to build it, in much the same way that proper British automobiles were built from the outset.  The classic lines and meticulous build, puts the car solidly into the executive class, yet the performance of the sporting automobile is there.    There is no equal to a Bentley – except, perhaps, its stablemate Rolls Royce.    For those not in the know, the Brooklands is known as one of the last of the greats from when Bentley were producing very small volume in Crewe. Today, Bentley builds almost 10 times the amount of vehicles on the same site, but use partners within VW group to facilitate these numbers by streamlining some of the production. This means that the only body structure that is built in Crewe today is for the Mulsanne, all others start their life in VW group plants where they are manufactured to our specifications.     The underpinnings of the Mulsanne are not too dissimilar from the Brooklands, the same 6.75 litre heart is used (albeit modernised) and interiors still use around 15 bull hides and lashings of oak to give the unique finish of a Bentley.    Beautiful straight body with very nice factory paintwork.    Mechanically sound and interior is stunning.    This is a car to be proud of.  Absolute magic to drive.    True that compared to today's cars, it doesn't feel like a sports car but for its day, it is quite sporting and performance oriented.    When you put your foot into it, even halfway down on the accelerator, the car really moves out, and it's extremely smooth.    The power line is smooth. The transmission is butter smooth but in our view, it's the seating position in the Bentley that makes it so different. From the outside it looks like a traditional car, but when you sit in it you sit high. You have a real commanding view of the road, and there's just nothing like it. description: Porsche Boxster S  This Porsche Boxster S is an uber rare find.  In 2004 Porsche wished to celebrate the 50th Anniversary of its legendary 550 Spyder and to do so delivered a limited and very special Boxster S. Worldwide only 1,953 cars were made and ours is one of those. A plaque in the centre consol confirms it is number 479 of this limited run.  We are unsure of the number of these cars that were officially imported to Australia, but it is fair to say it would be very few. This is a cherished and collectable Porsche with few signs of wear.   Make no mistake this is not a simple exercise in putting a celebratory badge on a car. Like the original 550 Spyder Porsche took full advantage of the Boxster’s already great handling owing to its mid-engine layout. What it then did is make several key modifications to make this special edition very special indeed. Power was increased from its 3.2 litre engine to 266 bhp, the manual 6 speed gearbox was improved to deliver a 15% increase in shift speed, the double stacked sports exhaust is unique to the car too. Handling was further sharpened using M030 sports suspension lowering the car by 10mm and 5mm wheel spacers were applied which improved the stance in a quite striking way. Indeed, larger wheels were also used as seen on the 911 Carrera and are painted in an attractive Seal Grey which contrasts with the special GT Silver metallic common to all these cars.  Externally other differences which demonstrate the attention to detail and lengths Porsche went to include the special badging chrome finish to the Boxster S badge and colour coding the air intakes.   Further additions were made to the interior including the use of excellent and very supportive quality leather bucket seats, the use of a steering wheel from the Porsche Turbo S, additional use of leather, chrome surrounds to the gauges amongst other quality touches. It feels like Porsche decided to go through the entire car and lift it to something quite special.  The interior is a lovely place to be with little evidence of wear. The full sports bucket seats are a real feature and high quality with colour coded silver shell backs.  Both front and rear storage spaces are immaculate.   Sitting in this car really is a visual treat and what you would expect from Porsche. The leather steering wheel is unmarked, the dials and dash are perfect to the eye and the gear knob and carpets show few signs of wear.  The hood works as it should and once down makes for a wonderful driving experience.  Everything is functioning correctly and out on the open road it is superb with the famous flat six delivering a fabulous sound coupled with the sharp handling.  Using a short throw 6-speed manual gearbox is a real treat. Its action has the precision of a well-engineered rifle bolt and is additive to use. The engine begs to be revved and makes this a genuinely competent and quick car and feels faster than its claimed 0-100 time of 5.7 seconds.  The owner has recently fitted Pirelli PZeros all round and the original wheels are virtually unmarked with only some small paint chips to just one wheel rim.  All the original books accompany the car along with its 2 sets of supplied keys. Service records and invoices are with the car too. Of note the IMS bearing was replaced as a precautionary measure ensuring confidence for the next custodian.  This car is just superb and a modern classic that would be right at home in a Porsche collection. We think these cars are real sleepers and very undervalued and now rightly being recognised for the wonderful cars they are. Now is the time to invest in the rarest version of this model. It’s on the button and ready for the next owner to enjoy some top-down motoring at its finest.

description: We are delighted to offer this truly incredible 1959 Austin Healey 3000.  Not only does it possess the design elegance which Healey’s are renowned for, but this example has been sensibly modified over the years by known Healey specialists to create an example that combines breath taking performance with features that make the driving experience a more comfortable one, including a 5-speed gearbox and air-conditioning.   As you can imagine with circa 245HP on tap, a huge amount has been invested in this car to bring it up to the standard it is now, and it is a car that has been meticulously ‘fettled’ to deliver exhilarating performance when asked but is reliable and perfectly at home touring extensive distances. Indeed, in recent Healey events it has travelled without fault, from the Gold Coast to Perth and back, to northern QLD and in this year from Melbourne to the Gold Coast.  The current owner who is a long-standing member of the Healey community has had this car for 7 years and unfortunately now needs to let the car go due to a medical condition preventing it being used.  Previous owners include a ‘who’s who’ in the Healey world.  We know Dave Woodhouse was an owner in the 70’s and 80’s. He was a renowned engine builder, and he owned the car and built a very capable engine back then.  Dave Dawson then purchased the car in the late 80s and instructed The Healey Factory to further modify this Healey including work to the suspension, brakes (all round discs), the fitment of the Heavy Duty Supra Gearbox, the air-conditioning and had the interior restored too. The original colour flash was also changed from red to blue.  Dave Dawson sold the car in 2009 to Gary Whitrod who in turn sold to Tony Rogers. In 2014 he commissioned further extensive modifications. Over a 2-year period some $80,000 was invested with PowerPlay in Melbourne, making this an incredibly capable car with its engine as the centre piece. Running on triple 45 Webers the 3275cc engine produces some 245HP at the flywheel and delivers thrilling performance. As you would imagine it has been carefully engineered to deliver this reliably with fitment of a large Aluminium radiator and upgraded cooling fan amongst numerous items.   A full and extensive record of this work accompanies the car.  Externally the car has been treated to new paint by the current owners in Old English White over Dark Blue. It is stunning and suits the car incredibly well. The car sits on 205 65/R15 Minilites that look purposeful and are in perfect order.   Once sat inside you are greeted by a dashboard that is simply gorgeous to the eye, and the cabin is simply a lovely place to be. The rare Smiths ‘Click’ Tachometer is particularly appealing to the eye. All the gauges work are clear and like new. Usefully a number of dash warning lights have been fitted to keep the driver informed. It has been reupholstered and the blue leather seats are in excellent order and work so well with the colour of the car. New carpeting was also fitted finishing off the internal space perfectly.   Turn the key are you really know this engine means business. It starts easily and settles into an even idle. Out on the open road the car is just superb. Interestingly all the controls and inputs are easy to use. The clutch is not heavy, the brakes are even in their application and very responsive and the 5-speed gearbox is a delight to use and its easy to work through the gears. The 3.5 differential makes it particularly easy for cruising speeds.  When you want to push on this car really is a thrill. The throttle responsive is immediate and the noise from that engine is addictive. It really does go and go and go. It would never fail to put a smile on your face.  The handling is impressive due in part to the fitment of Koni adjustable shock absorbers, 4-wheel power disc brakes and much investment in the suspension. The steering response is immediate and unusually good. The whole package is adds up to a car that is pin sharp in every respect.  To finish the car off perfectly it comes with a matching factory hard top, soft top and tonneau made from matching blue Mercedes material and side screens which are like new.  The air-conditioning is a wonderful feature of this car allowing it to become a comfortable tourer when required. It works incredibly well.  In summary this Healey is a truly special car. Its perfectly at home as a tourer; comfortable, practical with plenty of torque and power on tap. When you want to indulge in some ‘spirited’ driving it delivers, in spades. This is one well appointed car with everything done and wants for nothing other than to be driven and enjoyed.  2 large folders of invoices and documents supporting its history accompany the car.

description: Update, need a Ute for my new gig, so would consider exchange, with cash my way. Only looking for a Toyota Luxy 4x4 LN172R X Cab, Diesel, turbo preferred, ‘97 - ‘03 manual. Max $14000. Heaps Rare Alpine White E30 325i Wagon Factory Manual. Too many cars so time to move the wagon onto a new collector. In possibly the best E30 colour combo, Alpine White on black. Grey leather seats, no rips or tears. Leather gear shift and gaitor. Dash is 99% clean, very rare in this vintage, only one minor crack a couple of cms in length, please see pic. Cargo cover and rare dog guard in full working order. Wheels recently renod and no gutter rash. Recently had $7000 spent, invoices will come with the car, to recommission and for the bluey. 12 Months Full Rego, expires July 2024. Sample of works done as follows: Cam Belt. Water Pump. Full Service - fluid change and radiator flush. Full Wheel alignment. New rotors, calipers and pads all round. Full braking system bleed and refill. New Rear Shocks. New Rear Sway Bar. Paint is pretty much original and comes up heaps well. No rust in the usual wagon areas, the rear luggage pockets, wheel arches, sills or under the screen, all clean. Stainless steel rear box, sounds throaty, not too loud. Full electric pack all fully working. Headlamp wash/wipe, the previous owner removed the wipers, all plumping and switches are intact. Sunroof also perfect, again no rust, a common area for failure. All gauges work as well as the OBC, again unusual in the vintage. Headliner was redone a few years and is still good, no sagging, a common area of failure in these wagons. No cracks on any bumper bars or plastic trims, very rare. description: Penned by Giorgetto Giugiaro at Bertone, the 105’s clean and distinctive design made it one of the most attractive small coupes of the 1960s and 70s and the earlier ‘Stepnose’ cars were the first of that body shape and seen as the most desirable. Of the ‘Stepnose’ shape the earliest pre ‘Veloce’ type are seen as the most sought after and this is one of those examples.  Our car was produced in 1965 and delivered new in August to London and this is confirmed by the Alfa Romeo Centro Documentazione which accompanies the car. There are UK records confirming previous owners with records showing mileage in 1981 was a mere 26,833 miles. The current reading is at just 28,513. The car remained in the UK until 2004 when it when it was bought into Brisbane and was found to be in remarkably good and original condition. The current owner acquired the car in 2020 and commissioned an exacting and full restoration which has been recently finished with less than 1,000 kms use since.   The current owner is offering it for sale due to lack of use and a wish to thin down his collection. This presents a great opportunity for the next owner to purchase the car at a fraction of the cost of the initial investment. Invoices which accompany the car total in excess of $90,000 which excludes the purchase price of the car itself.  The quality of body is just perfect and was subject to a full strip and paint by one of the best in the business. Once the paint was removed the shell was found to be in incredibly good condition with very little metal requiring replacement, this reflecting the sheltered life the car has benefitted from.  It was decided to repaint the car in the period correct ‘Medio Grigio Metallizato’ rather than its original Verde Muschio. This brighter colour looks absolutely stunning with the original interior colour of ‘Choio’. It suits the car very well and is very appealing to the eye. The paint is flawless, and the work to the body is documented and comes with the car.  Turn the key and the engine fires up with a familiar Alfa Romeo growl. It has been rebuilt and running without fault. Out on the open road this car is superb and it’s easy to understand why its handling humbled many sports cars of its era (and for many years later).  The gearbox has been disassembled, inspected and where necessary any parts replaced. As a result it is easy to use and everything performs as expected.  Once inside, the cabin feels light and airy and a nice place to be. The dashboard is like new and is a real feature of the car. Everything works as it should with every guage completely restored. The seats still retain their original fabric except for 2 replacement panels. They are in excellent condition and the interior is a real feature of this car. The owner has had desirable ‘box weave’ carpets made and these look stunning adding a real quality finish. The boot has a replacement light grey rubber mat as fitted in period. Like much of this car it is as new.  The headlining has been replaced and is the correct type.  The wheels are the original and have been refurbished. All the brightwork has been polished at great expense and works beautifully with the metallic grey paint. The engine bay is pin sharp and presents as new. Even the correct stickers have been traced and used for items such as the radiator and brake booster.  As you would expect the underside of the car presents is as clean and fresh as it is on top.  Overall, this represents a spectacular first series ‘Stepnose’ with a huge amount of work done and significant investment made. This would be a perfect buy for someone considering restoring a car but wishing to avoid the wait or costs! A wonderfully attractive car and definitive classic Alfa Romeo.

description: This rare 1976 XJ4.2 Coupe was Australian Delivered in 1977 to Brysons in Adelaide SA. It presents in immaculate condition with an accompanying thick service history file including photographic evidence of an earlier rebuild. Resplendently glorious in its original Colour of Old English white with Velour Interior in a delightful shade of Fawn, makes a truly impressive and enjoyable place to spend time in on long drives in Grand tourer fashion. Recently recommissioned after a short period of layup with extensive recent work totalling over $10,000, leaving nothing for her new owner other than to drive and enjoy, a further benefit to the documented low 27,000 Kilometres with original matching numbers engine, fully rebuilt during an earlier restoration. I’ve recently put over 1,000 issue free miles where the reliability and performance from this work completed has proven all the money spent has been worth it. Every bush, rubber and suspension component has been replaced, front and rear, resulting in a quiet rattle free waft, exactly as Jaguar engineered this girl to drive 50 years ago. 4 new original style mufflers sound delightful at idle as she starts up instantly and settles into a quiet burble. Push her a little from cruising speed and she responds rapidly without fuss or over exertion with just a little more of that quiet burble but never intrusive into the luxurious cocoon. She pulls away without hesitation, with an impressive oil pressure staying constant and temperature rarely varying even on hot days and big uphill climbs with the air conditioner running and even when the engine pushed a little harder to maintain cruising speeds on mountain roads. Steering is accurate without any slop in the steering attesting again to the rigorous attention given to replaced suspension componentry. This 4.2 has no skuttle shake or jitters on nasty roads and soaks everything up without wallowing or diving in corners. Inside the walnut dash still shines and is in perfect condition from the restoration in the early 2000s, when the Australian Jaguar XJ Coupe register described her as being in Usable Concours condition. The air conditioning is cold and on a hot day cools down the cabin after sitting in the sun within mere moments. All the switches on the dash work, the electric windows all glide up and down as they originally did from the factory, according to my Jaguar specialist, better than any other he has seen in years and the steering wheel sits perfectly centred following the wheel alignment after all the suspension work. The clock quietly ticks away and keeps perfect time with that unique Jaguar sound. Most of the Old English white Coupes came with Red interiors. If that is a bit over the top in your eyes, then you’ll love the subtle shade of the much rarer Fawn. The velour has survived extremely well attesting to her low milage, which would be hard to find on any of the leather examples, and it is also a much nicer place to sit in the soft velour. Forget about sheep skins, these seats simply don’t need to be covered for comfort as leather seats most often are and it would be a shame not to enjoy sitting on the much rarer velvety velour. The overall upholstery finish throughout the interior of the car is outstanding, with only a few minor character blemishes to be expected from a surviving interior approaching 50 years old. The Radio Cassette is an original AWA Clarion AM/FM working from both front door speakers. The shut lines, body work and panels are pristine, the paintwork beautiful, chrome work original, neat as a pin and sparkling. While glass is all original and without scratches, the windscreen also includes the original window sticker with identifying numbers. The car has however, benefitted from an extensive rebuild in 2000 after a previous 13 years in storage, with maintenance receipts covering her full-service history back to this time. All opening panels hinge with a well oiled silent stiffness and doors close with a soft push and lovely click, as all replaced rubbers seals have now settled in. A good sign considering how many of these old girls with much higher miles can be worn out from holding up a big heavy panels. The Vinyls roof was replaced during the rebuild, with photographs of the work, and is still like new today with no rust bubbles or any of the shabbiness often encountered with an old Jag. On the contrary, even the underside is exquisite, with any inspection welcomed, it would be hard to find much more than a couple of age related character marks anywhere. The brakes that have had recent work pull up sharply and in a straight line. Correct wheels and trims are in lovely condition and the Hankook Optimo K406 225/60r15 tires while not new, have most of their tread left and provide decent grip. The engine bay tells a story of well cared for originality. There are no leaks, all hoses are in great shape, ignition leads while not brand new are fine. Often the carburettors were changed to SUs, but here we have the original twin Strombergs which have been tuned and run perfectly. The fuels tanks have been flushed and both send accurate readings to the fuel gauge. The rebuilt engine has only a little over 27,000 kms and excellent compression on all cylinders which was rebuilt using standard size rings, pistons and bearings, when it had its mechanicals overhauled in 2001, with photos, invoices and receipts for the rebuild still retained in her file. Most Jag mechanics will tell you, these 4.2 litre straight sixes are much easier to work on with lower maintenance bills than the V12 alternative. Clearly benefiting from specialist attention and lots of love lavished over her life, this delightful Coupe is now ready to be enjoyed by her next custodian. Supplied with 3 full sets of Keys and an original Series 2 Coupe Operating, Maintenance and Service Handbook included, along with a thick history file and old photos. Gorgeous and rarer than E Type Jaguar, valued and insured for $68,000 a fair asking price for a lovely car which drives like new and would be very difficult to find in such good condition for any less. Forget about trying to restore anything lesser for even close as it would cost hundreds of thousands. I have seen the really good condition exceptions like this one sell for more than this asking price in the last few years.

description: THE STORY  Unveiled in the fall of 1977 and hitting the roads in 1978, the Ferrari 308 GTS quickly became one of the most iconic models in the legendary Italian marque’s history. Designed by the renowned Pininfarina studio and engineered by Ferrari’s in-house team, the 308 GTS set a new standard for high-performance mid-engine sports cars.  The GTS designation stood for ``Gran Turismo Spider,`` emphasizing its convertible roof that could be removed or stowed, offering a pure and open-air driving experience.  The Ferrari 308 GTS was powered by a 2.9-liter, quad-cam V8 engine capable of producing 255 horsepower. Paired with a five-speed manual transmission, the car offered sharp handling and superb agility, making it one of the most exciting Ferraris of its time. Its unique mid-engine layout ensured optimal weight distribution, delivering exceptional balance through tight corners and open highways alike.  The car’s success was further solidified with its starring role in the popular television series ‘Magnum P.I.” where it captured the imagination of a global audience.  As the 1970s drew to a close, the Ferrari 308 GTS firmly entrenched itself as one of the most admired and enduring sports cars in the world - blending stunning looks with exceptional performance and continuing to uphold Ferrari's prestigious legacy.    THE CAR  Originally sold new in California USA, this beautiful example of a 1978 Ferrari 308 GTS was imported to Australia in the 1990s by a previous owner. The car was converted to right-hand drive in 2002 by Prestige Auto Care in South Australia. Conversions to right hand drive are believed to have been mandatory at that time as the car was less than 30 years old.   The car has also undergone a full nut and bolt restoration which was completed in 2014. This included a bare metal respray in her original Rosso Corsa red paint and new interior trim. The car looks as good today as it did when the restoration work was completed.  The current owner has enjoyed the car since 2018 and under his stewardship, the gearbox has been rebuilt, the car has had an “engine out” service, the Weber carburettors have been professionally tuned, new radiator hoses have been fitted, and the car’s wiring harness and air conditioning have both been upgraded.   The car’s paint presents beautifully as does the upholstery, gauges, dash, switches and steering wheel. The targa top is in excellent condition and is very simple to remove. All electrics work and the car has a complete tool kit.  Getting behind the wheel of this 308 GTS is everything you’d expect – from the famed bark of the Ferrari V8 engine, right through to the gated gear changes and precision handling that will leave you grinning from ear to ear.  The car also has 4 x additional factory rims that will be made available to the purchaser at an additional cost. T  his extremely well-sorted Ferrari is in outstanding condition.

The MGB was in production until 1980, with over half a million built and over 400,000 of these going to the important North American market. For battery preservation a ‘kill’ switch has been fitted an CTEK trickle charger is included.      Unlike the earlier rubber bumper MG B's, this 1977 B is fitted with the factory revised suspension geometry, allowing the taller ride height, without compromising road-holding, while further improving the ride through greater suspension travel and ground clearance. description: The Jaguar 2.4 was the first post-war small Jaguar and in many ways still the most significant.    Powered by a small bore XK engine, it was the first Jag to use a modern monocoque construction and started a range that became the mainstay of the company, selling in large numbers and attracting a younger clientele.    Originally known just as the 2.4 and 3.4, this range later became referred to as the MK1 in 1960 after the MK2 was launched a year earlier. Although most enthusiasts regard the MK2 as the Jaguar to have, the MK1 was a revelation in its day. They’re very similar to the MK2 – indeed there’s more purity to the design and style. And let’s face it, they’re different and a lot rarer than the MK2!    ABOUT THIS CAR        Heritage Certificate Available      Restored - very straight body clean of rust with excellent paintwork.      Interior - upholstery, carpets in very good condition - most beautiful woodwork.      White wall tires.      Mechanically sound - Car drives beautifully.      Circa 121139 Miles      This car is in very nice condition - it 's an excellent performer and has a most beautiful note to it.      MK1s are pretty hard to find due to their rarity and are still valued less than a MK2, but the gap is closing as an increasing number of cat lovers are seeing the MK1 in a new light.    The burning question is how does a MK1 compare to the MK2?    Well, while they both handled reasonably well for their time, things have changed enormously in over half a century. Driven appropriately, the Mk1 can be extremely rewarding in its own right with adequate performance, even though the 2.4 was deemed sluggish by Jaguar once the meatier 3.4 arrived on the scene.    The MK1 is almost as refined as the its successor on the move and the sight of that handsome XK-style, four-spoked Bluemell steering wheel and centered instruments is enough to woo any MK2 die-hard.    Great cars - Great value - Great investment like any 60's Jag. Our view is that finding the right MK1 will take time and dedication but because of its rarity, this will be a car to keep in the knowledge that it will appreciate far more than its more popular MK2 relative.    If you’ve been hankering after a MK2, then just try the original first – you may well prefer it. description:
Ordered at the end of 1934, this Rolls-Royce was delivered to coachbuilder Barker in London to receive Touring Limousine bodywork, with some special order instructions and delivered to its first owners in Scotland, in 1935.

They retained the elegant car for 22 years, and the following Scottish owner also kept it 22 years before it was shipped to Canada. Following many years of ownership there the car moved to New Zealand before finally coming to Western Australia. The current, 6th owner bought it locally and has enjoyed the car for the past eight years.

It has been notably reliable and in frequent use (which is beneficial to any older Rolls-Royce). This has included in displays and country runs, including to Lake Perkolilli, just beyond Kalgoorlie where it has participated in the event there – twice. The car runs smoothly and provides a comfortable and effortless drive as intended by its designers.

Remarkably, this car has never been restored. The paintwork is original and well worn, the ‘patina’ giving the car great character. With aluminium bodywork there’s no rust. The front seat has been reupholstered and the extensive polished woodwork refinished, but the remainder of the interior remains original. Occasional seats are fitted to the rear compartment and stow below the glass division.

The car has its original wheel covers, but the owner prefers the look of the wire wheels. The number plates 1935 RR will go with the car to a WA buyer.

This Rolls-Royce has clearly always been well maintained and thus has proven absolutely reliable for the owner.

description:
This car has been comprehensively rebuilt for multiple uses. As a country cruising car, as a competition car and as a club car.

Acquired by the current owner almost twenty years ago, a six year restoration was completed in 2012.

For the comfort angle, the car would be fitted with later type GT6 seats with headrests, trimmed in cream leather. The rest of the interior was trimmed and carpeted to match, with “Jaguar” carpets. Beneath is sound deadening material.

The owner’s intention was to create a car his wife could drive and which could also be used in club level motorsport events. Thus, a more powerful version of the Triumph 6-cylinder unit was built-up for the car. At 2.5 litres, with fuel injection the car’s power output is 130bhp. A stronger gearbox from a Triumph sedan is fitted, with electric overdrive.

Some $40,000 was spent on the build and when finished, the car began appearing at club events. At the Triumph Nationals, it was voted runner-up in the People’s Choice award. Upgrades to the suspension and brakes while refining the car for events saw an additional $12,000 spent.

The result is a potent, predictable sporty coupe which has competed in Albany Round the Houses events, track days at Wanneroo raceway with the VSCC and competed in motorkhanas with the Triumph club. The GT6 has attended Triumph Nationals in 2014, 2018 and 2024. It’s won several trophies…

There’s a Heritage Certificate with this car. The selling dealer was Premier Motors in Perth, WA state distributor for Triumph.

The rebuild was completed some years ago now and there’s the odd chip and blister, but overall it still presents very well. The GT6 drives very well, as one might expect after such a sorting campaign.

If the car sells to a Western Australian buyer the number plates GT6 will be available for $1000, otherwise standard issue plates will be provided.

The owner advises that the car has been very reliable and is keen to point out that it has no oil leaks and never runs hot. On the road it quickly becomes evident that while the car offers plenty of grunt, it can be docile and easy to use in traffic. It’s ready for use as a weekend fun car or in club motorsports.

Mercedes-Benz has a long history of making elegant coupe versions of its luxury sedan models. This is a fine example of the W124 series, being the late version 320CE, which is quite rare and desirable.

The W124 series is legendary for its high quality of engineering and build quality. The 3.2-litre 6-cylinder engine is known for its smoothness and this car doesn’t disappoint. The car drives exceptionally well, with a nice tight feel that a well-kept example can exhibit. This beautifully kept pillarless coupe has covered just 196,000km.

An Australian-delivered car, it was first sold in Sydney. The stamped service booklet, among all the factory booklets, shows the car’s service history prior to being purchased by the current owner who shipped the car to Perth three years ago. He undertook some minor work since, details of which can be provided.

The car has had rear parking sensors added as well as a dimming interior mirror. It wears good Michelin Energy tyres.

This 320CE is a beautiful example in excellent condition. The bodywork is straight with very good paint. The external hardware is all good.

Inside, the comfortable interior is also excellent with all fittings in very good condition.

The colour scheme suits this elegant coupe very well too. It’s the desirable updated model with the larger engine and several other tweaks with which Mercedes-Benz kept the model at the top of the W124 ladder – and these come onto the market rarely. Don’t miss your chance

The car remains in its original paint colours of British Racing Green Body and cream wire spoke wheels. At the time of purchase, the car was in very good condition for its age, with the speedometer at 74,000 Mls, which was genuine. Restoration included mechanical (full engine rebuild and components deemed necessary for overhaul/replacement) completed by Mike Roddy (Jaguar Specialist). Additional electrical and interior work was completed, as well as full body respray. Recently 4 new tyres have been fitted.
